articles.title: Bill Belichick gives first comments since GM Michael Lombardi's resignation, allegations against UNC football program
articles.summary: Belichick wasn't able to speak about the investigation, but assured the media that he has control over the program.
articles.body:
North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick spoke to the media on Monday for the first time since the details of the various investigations into the program came to light .

UNC announced Thursday that general manager Michael Lombardi had resigned amid a human resources complaint filed against the football program. A subsequent report from Raleigh TV station WRAL indicated questions around potential drug use by UNC defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, Bill's son.

At the start of the news conference on Monday, it was announced that, because the investigations are ongoing, neither Belichick nor the players would be able to speak about them.

Belichick addressed the situation briefly.

"[We] understand the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team. And obviously our high standard of our code of conduct, doing things the right way, and making sure that our student athletes are given the utmost, best treatment, best care and very best coaching that we can possibly give them, so that's critically important to us."

"[We] understand the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team.

And obviously our high standard of our code of conduct, doing things the right way, and making sure that our student athletes are given the utmost, best treatment, best care and very best coaching that we can possibly give them, so that's critically important to us."

Belichick was asked if his program had an atmosphere of compliance. His answer was, "Yeah, totally," and he didn't expand or add any further details.

Reporter Pat Welter of WRAL tried to ask about the investigation, but when Belichick reminded them that he couldn't speak on the investigation, the reporter rephrased and asked: "What indications do we have, based on the last year and everything that has been reported, that you have control of this program?"

Belichick again was brief and responded, "If you were around here every day, I think you'd see it."

He then went on to brief the media on the Tar Heels' upcoming game against East Tennessee State University on Saturday. When asked how Steve Belichick was doing, the head coach confirmed that he was still on medical leave.

Steve has been away from the program since Aug. 6. All that Bill said about the situation when it was announced was that "Steve is on medical leave. We look forward to getting him back as soon as possible." The defensive coordinator did not make the trip to Dublin for UNC's win over TCU to begin the season. UNC did not have a game this past weekend.

The head coach had no updates on hiring a new general manager or replacing his son as defensive coordinator. The press conference was dominated by questions about the investigation, but Belichick ensured that he didn't say anything he wasn't permitted to, not giving much to those in attendance.

UNC's football program has been under scrutiny since before the season began. There was an internal investigation into Lombardi before he resigned.

Lombardi was reportedly investigated by the university over allegations related to an HR dispute involving a former UNC front office employee.

The program is also dealing with a secondary investigation . Steve Belichick is reportedly being looked at after claims that he may have used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player.

A separate investigation is concerned with whether a member of UNC's recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player. Similarly, there is an investigation into whether there were possible sexual relationships between assistant coaches and recruiting staff.

The investigations could be a distraction for the program, but that wasn't evident in the Week 0 win over TCU in Dublin. The Tar Heels will look to improve to 2-0 as they take on ETSU on Saturday.

articles.title: Alerta roja en el Coliseum
articles.standfirst: El Celta es incapaz de remontar a un Getafe con diez y el punto deja tocados a ambos
articles.summary: El Celta es incapaz de remontar a un Getafe con diez y el punto deja tocados a ambos
articles.body: Getafe y Celta salieron del Coliseum alimentando las dudas que les acompañan en este inicio de temporada. Aguantó el equipo de Bordalás con uno menos, por expulsión de Romero, pero suma una victoria en cuatro jornadas. Y le resultó imposible al equipo celeste, que todavía no sabe lo que es ganar en esta liga. Un punto de insatisfacción que refuerza las malas sensaciones de ambos. Dentro de ese sabor agridulce, es el equipo azulón que se acerca más a lo que quiere y debe ser esta temporada. Abraza algunas certezas, el estilo se mantiene y Bordalás empieza a tener una idea aproximada de su once ideal. Todo lo contrario que un Celta donde Giráldez mantiene sus rotaciones continuas y el equipo insinúa pero no concreta. Funciona, de momento, a fogonazos y con apariciones puntuales brillantes, pero sin que esa finura se mantenga a lo largo de un partido. En ese escenario, donde el Celta dominó por momentos, siempre sobresalió Hugo González. Es la mejor noticia de los gallegos en este inicio de temporada. Suya fue la primera ocasión, que desbarató Soria, y suyo fue siempre el protagonismo en el último tercio de campo. A ese remate que respondió el hombre récord del Getafe encontró alternativa en la otra portería Terrats, el más destacado de los azulones durante el primer tiempo. Lo hizo todo bien hasta que erró en un mano a mano que dificultó el oficio de Starfelt, estorbando lo justo en el momento del remate. Estaba el partido buscando gobernante cuando Satriano cazó un balón suelto a la salida de un córner. Estiró el pie tras un rechace que le cayó en el área pequeña y el Getafe encontró refuerzo moral para su plan de juego. Sin embargo, en otro balón aéreo encontró la solución un Celta que merecía mejor suerte. Starfelt remató en plancha un centro de Hugo González, quién si no, para resetear el choque. No era el partido de una dureza extrema pero lo cierto es que Romero cambió todo con dos entradas inoportunas que condenaron al Getafe a jugar con uno menos en el último tramo del partido. La segunda se la sacó Hugo González, de nuevo con un punto de velocidad extra para generar desequilibrio. De poco sirvió que Giráldez acabase el partido con Borja Iglesias y Jutglá sobre el césped. La acumulación de rematadores sirvió de más bien poco. Fue el quiero y no puedo que manifestó el equipo gallego a lo largo de todo el encuentro en el Coliseum. Una impotencia aderezada por ese instinto de supervivencia eterna que exhibe la marca Bordalás en el sur de Madrid. Un punto escaso, angustioso, para dos equipos que miran a Europa de reojo mientras se complican la vida en el torneo doméstico. Un clásico de cada temporada en nuestra liga. No es para estar preocupados, todavía, pero sí algo inquietos.

articles.title: Satriano: "En el Getafe, el trabajo no se negocia"
articles.standfirst: Criticó la dureza del árbitro contra Zaid en la doble amarilla
articles.summary: Criticó la dureza del árbitro contra Zaid en la doble amarilla
articles.body: Martín Satriano, jugador uruguayo del Getafe y autor del gol de su equipo en el empate frente al Celta (1-1), destacó el "tremendo trabajo" del conjunto azulón y aseguró que el esfuerzo es una obligación que "no se negocia" a las órdenes de José Bordalás. "Estoy contento por el gol. Al final, el empate no era lo que queríamos, pero, por cómo se dio el partido, lo agarramos y ya estamos pensando en el siguiente", declaró a Movistar Plus+. También lamentó las circunstancias que condicionaron al Getafe durante la segunda parte, especialmente la expulsión de Zaid Romero por doble amonestación. "El córner, la roja, dos amarillas muy justas... Esos detalles te condicionan. Hoy en día es muy difícil jugar diez contra once. Seguimos adelante, pensando en el siguiente partido y en trabajar", afirmó. Satriano terminó el encuentro con problemas físicos, aunque restó importancia a sus dolores: "Es una pequeña molestia que venía arrastrando, pero estoy bien. No es nada grave", tranquilizó. También ensalzó el esfuerzo colectivo frente al Celta: "Creo que todos hicimos un tremendo trabajo. El Celta es un gran equipo y eso, en el Getafe, no se negocia en ningún partido". Por último, señaló la importancia de convertir el Coliseum en una garantía de puntos después de sumar una victoria y un empate en los dos encuentros disputados como local. "Tenemos que hacernos fuertes en casa. Para los rivales no es fácil venir a jugar aquí y es bueno que sea así. Ahora tenemos otro partido en casa, contra el Deportivo, y hay que aprovecharlo para sumar", concluyó.

articles.title: Bordalás: “El presi sabe que no hemos hecho bien el trabajo”
articles.standfirst: El técnico alicantino, sobre el mercado de fichajes del Geta
articles.summary: El técnico alicantino, sobre el mercado de fichajes del Geta
articles.body: José Bordalás comparecía en sala de prensa tras el empate frente al Celta este lunes. Satisfecho con el resultado, devolvía el recado al presidente que en la previa aseguró que la plantilla es justa pero completa y se han hecho dos fichajes. "La plantilla se quedó corta, yo insisto, con muchos chavales del filial, con uno menos prefería tener en el campo jugadores con más experiencia, y eran demasiado jóvenes. Al presi le toca decir eso pero sabe que nos hemos quedado cortos y no se ha hecho bien el trabajo". El alicantino, preguntado por las expulsiones esta temporada, señaló que le parecía “injusto”, sobre todo haciendo referencia a la de Zaid Romero: “Solo ha hecho dos faltas”. Valoración: “El equipo ha hecho méritos, entró bien, estuvo serio, hemos competido bien. Nos han empatado en balón parado, pero no perdimos la cara. En esas dos faltas, las únicas que ha hecho Zaid, cuanto menos es extraño. No es un jugador que haya hecho muchas faltas y por reiteración a veces se sacan esas tarjetas. Aun así, el equipo ha sido muy competitivo, muy solidario, ha sabido defender ese resultado, hemos tenido una ocasión de Andrés cuando Enes estaba solo para empujarla. Me quedo con el esfuerzo y el trabajo del equipo”. Tres expulsiones: “Eso es lo que hago habitualmente, no esta temporada, llevo muchas así. Al final tampoco son acciones agresivas, no son acciones que puedan merecer la expulsión. Tampoco son del todo justas, no voy a hablar, solo de las acciones, no son justas. A nosotros es evidente que no se nos trata de la misma manera”. Kiko Femenía: “Parece que tiene una lesión, se tendrán que hacer las pruebas, ha notado un pinchazo en el isquio y no podía seguir”. Cambios: “Simplemente había jugadores que parecía que estaban para cambiarlo, les consultábamos si podían continuar, algunos nos dijeron que aguantaban, otros no podían. Intentábamos y con uno menos, la última ventana, no queríamos hacer un cambio y que luego pudiéramos quedarnos con nueve. Hemos apurado hasta tener la certeza, porque han hecho un esfuerzo grande. Han sabido sufrir como Mojica, Enes, estaban muy limitados de fuerzas”. Jugadores cansados: “Indudablemente, nos hemos visto en la obligación de jugar con los mismos jugadores, incluso la previa de Conference, han tenido que jugar domingo y jueves. Estábamos muy rotos, los que han llegado han llegado a última hora, hay jugadores con meses y tiempo sin competir. Se está pagando el esfuerzo”.

articles.title: Baggio, el último héroe del Inter ante el Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Autor de la victoria en Champions en 1998, última vez que derrotaron en Copa de Europa al equipo blanco
articles.summary: Autor de la victoria en Champions en 1998, última vez que derrotaron en Copa de Europa al equipo blanco
articles.body: Roberto Baggio, Balón de Oro en 1993, fue el gran protagonista de la última victoria del Inter ante el Real Madrid, en 1998 en San Siro, cuando marcó dos goles en los últimos minutos para darle al equipo italiano un triunfo por 3-1 en la Liga de Campeones. El partido, disputado el 25 de noviembre de 1998, correspondió a la fase de grupos de la 'Champions' y enfrentó a dos equipos que partían entre los favoritos. El Inter llegaba a la cita con una plantilla en la que destacaban, entre otros, el propio Baggio, el brasileño Ronaldo o Diego Pablo Simeone, mientras que el Real Madrid contaba con una generación liderada por jugadores como Roberto Carlos, Clarence Seedorf, Raúl González o Manolo Sanchís. El conjunto italiano se adelantó en el marcador por medio de un exmadridista como el chileno Iván Zamorano y el Madrid empató rápidamente con gol de Seedorf. El Inter reaccionó y terminó dando la vuelta al encuentro, con Baggio, 'Il Divin Codino' (La Divina Coleta), como revulsivo y decisivo. El italiano igualó el marcador y, cuando el partido encaraba sus últimos minutos, volvió a aparecer para completar su doblete y establecer el definitivo 3-1. Sus dos tantos en el tramo final convirtieron a Baggio en el nombre propio de aquella noche en San Siro. La victoria tiene ahora un significado especial para el Inter, ya que desde entonces el conjunto italiano no ha vuelto a derrotar al Real Madrid en la Liga de Campeones. Los enfrentamientos posteriores entre ambos equipos han tenido un balance favorable al conjunto español, que se ha impuesto en las cuatro últimas citas europeas. Baggio había llegado al Inter ese mismo año después de su etapa en el Bolonia y afrontaba una temporada importante en su carrera. El desenlace convirtió a Baggio en el héroe de una de las noches europeas más recordadas de San Siro. Ahora, el Inter vuelve a medirse al Real Madrid con el objetivo de romper esa racha y recuperar una victoria que se le resiste desde aquella noche de 1998 en San Siro.

articles.title: USA vs. Czechia winners and losers as Breanna Stewart, vets bounce back
articles.summary: Team USA finished the group stage at the 2026 FIBA Basketball Women's World Cup with a dominant victory over Czechia. Here are the winners and losers.
articles.body:
Team USA finished group stage at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup with a 105-64 victory over Czechia Monday on Sept. 7 in Berlin, Germany.

The Americans improved to 3-0 at the Women's World Cup , completing a sweep of Group D. The 41-point victory is the USA's 33rd consecutive World Cup win, a streak that dates back to 2006.

Team USA was coming off a 55-52 victory over Italy on Sunday, the Americans' lowest point total at the World Cup since 1984. They bounced back with six players in double figures against Czechia. Breanna Stewart led Team USA with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists in 17 minutes. Angel Reese added 13 points, Napheesa Collier and Jackie Young 12 each and Paige Bueckers and Sonia Citron 10 each.

"I thought it was a great response that we had from yesterday's game. Obviously, we didn't shoot well, but coming out with the aggression that we did, especially on defense, I thought our on ball defense was pretty good," Collier said. "I saw a lot of people got their hands in."

The Americans advance to the quarterfinals and will play the winner of Japan-Hungary on Thursday, Sept. 10. Here are the winners and losers USA vs. Czechia:

Team USA women ready to make noise at FIBA World Cup

The "Young and Turnt" crew may be the future of Team USA, but the team's experienced core of veterans proved they are the present. With nine first-time players in the World Cup, the veterans reset the standard for the rookies to follow on Monday. That's exactly what they did.

USA's experienced core set the tone early, with Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier combining for 25 points in the first half. Stewart finished with 19 points, seven rebonds and six assists in 17 minutes in the win.

"I wanted to come out and really lead this team in a number of ways," said Stewart, the player of the game. "We wanted to make sure today we really took things into our own hands and really lead by example."

Stewart, a three-time Olympic gold medalist, is appearing in her fourth World Cup, joining Sue Bird (5) and Diana Taurasi (4) as the only American women to make at least four appearances. If USA goes on to win gold, Stewart will tie Bird for the most World Cup gold medals.

After USA survived Italy's nail-biting comeback bid, USA head coach Kara Lawson was candid with her newly-formed team. She challenged their passion, ability to compete and intensity, which should be a given representing the red, white and blue.

"Let this be the last time that a team plays with more passion than us throughout the course of the game," Lawson said. "Let this be the last time that all 12 (players) don't show up to compete at a high level. And then let this be the last time that we lack a resilient mindset because we're so upset that we're not scoring the way we're normally scoring. Your contribution has to be your effort, your passion, your energy, your intensity that you play with."

There was no question the Americans wanted to win on Monday. USA came out motivated, responding with a 41-point margin of victory against Czechia, their largest win of the tournament. Every USA player scored in the matchup.

"I knew our offense would come around. I'm so pleased with the way they are playing. Their effort and energy," Lawson said at halftime. "That was good to see."

Kiki Iriafen proved you always have to stay ready. After logging a DNP in USA's win over Italy on Sunday, head coach Kara Lawson called Iriafen's number in Monday's matchup against Czechia. Her impact was immediately felt. Iriafen recorded five points and 11 rebounds, including six on the offensive glass, plus one steal in eight minutes of work.

Team USA couldn't buy a basket from long range in Sunday's game against Italy as the Americans shot 1-of-12 from beyond the arc. The U.S. bounced back on Monday as Breanna Stewart knocked down a 3-pointer with 9:09 remaining in the first quarter to open scoring for the Americans.

Team USA had five 3s in the first half and finished 7-for-25. Seven different players made a 3-pointer in the game.

"We took some strides in transition offense," USA coach Kara Lawson said. "I thought we made some strides in our half court offensive execution, and our defensive awareness."

Czechia getting bounced from the tournament

Let's not mince words, the United States did not play well against Italy. The pulled it together against Czechia, making three consecutive 3-pointers to open the game and going on a 13-4 run to take a 14-point lead after the first quarter.

Czechia finished the tournament 0-3, losing to Italy and China in Group D play.

"We played against the best of the best, the United States," Czechia head coach Romana Ptáčková said. "It was really tough. We knew that, we knew that it's going to be hard in a low post and they showed us that."

Czechia was outrebounded 55-35 by the U.S. and outscored 52-30 in the paint. Czechia also committed 16 turnovers.

Monday was a rough day for Czechia guard Eliska Joklova. Hours ahead of Czechia's matchup against the USA, the Minnesota Lynx announced they were waiving Joklova to make room for newly-signed guard Aari McDonald. Czechia went on to suffer a 41-point loss to USA to add insult to injury. Joklova had a team-high 19 points in the loss, the only Czech player to reach double digits, but it was nowhere near enough to keep up with the Americans.

Team USA took care of the ball in the first half with zero turnovers in the first quarter and just two at halftime. The second half was a different story with 11 turnovers. Czechia scored 11 points off America's mistakes.

"We're improving every day. ... Every day that we're together, we're getting understanding of how to play off of one another, even how to communicate off of one another," USA coach Kara Lawson said.

Look for that communication to lead to less turnovers as the tournament progresses toward the medal round.
authors: Heather Burns and Cydney Henderson, USA TODAY

articles.title: Texas and Ohio State are treating Saturday like any other game. It really won't be
articles.summary: The Longhorns have lost to Ohio State twice in two seasons. Now Texas hosts the No. 1 Buckeyes in a game both teams call just another test.
articles.body:
Call the matchup between Texas and Ohio State a game of equals. OK, almost equals.

Hey, it has been a minute since the Longhorns have won it all. Well, more than a minute. Been 21 years, in fact . The Buckeyes were crowned champs more recently, like 20 months ago.

The Longhorns are fully acquainted with the Scarlet and Gray because Ohio State has beaten Texas twice in the last two seasons.

The first loss came in the College Football Playoff semifinals in the Cotton Bowl in January of 2025 and cost Texas a spot in the title game. Blame it on a toss sweep . The second loss last August kept the Longhorns out of the playoffs entirely although a 4-8 Florida team had something to do with it, too.

You would think the Longhorns would be foaming at the mouth to have another crack at the Big Ten's best ( sorry, Mr. Cignetti) . They probably are in the privacy of the locker room but were on their absolute best behavior Monday.

"I'm excited to get to play Ohio State," quarterback Arch Manning said. "This is why you come to a school like Texas, to play in these big-time games. We're excited."

So Arch is excited. I lost count at 10 of how many times the quarterback said he was excited.

Lance Jackson is excited, too, up to a point.

"I definitely feel like it's just like another game," the sophomore edge rusher said.

Uh, right, Lance. That's why Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said 20 million viewers will probably be tuned in to the 6:30 game Saturday night at Royal-Memorial Stadium to see just another game. Sure, just another non-conference game.

"We're going to prepare just like we did last week for Texas State," Jackson continued. "You kind of just treat it like last week. We're going to treat this week like next week and the next week after that. You don't really look at an (opposing) team and be like, I may practice harder this week."

There wasn't one disparaging word said about Ohio State. Well, former Buckeye Hero Kanu did acknowledge, "I'm not going to make it personal. Can't make it bigger than it is. Obviously, it's still a big game, but you can't let it get to your head. I went to Ohio State and have a lot of friends on that team. And not friends this week."

Of course, he means Texas isn't going to change the way it goes about its business to prepare for arguably the most consistent and successful football team in the country. The Longhorns haven't been far from becoming that with two close losses to the Buckeyes, but they do need to do something different to get over the hump.

"We believe in our process," Sarkisian said. "We've been very efficient in that. We've won a lot of big games since 2022. We won more Top 25 games than anyone. So we've been used to playing big games. We haven't won them all, but for the most part, we've performed pretty well."

He's right. Three straight seasons with 10 wins or more, but that's now how the Buckeyes define success.

It is safe to say this may be the biggest measuring stick for each this season, even if it is just Week 2 in September.

Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby put it best when he said, "It's Goliath against Goliath."

Texas versus Ohio State could well be the Game of the Year. Unless it was already the Ole Miss-Louisville thriller on Sunday night when defense was optional.

Nothing says college football quite like the Buckeyes and the Longhorns. Ohio State has 991 wins in history, second only to Michigan's 1,022, give or take depending on who the clock operator is. Texas has 972 and ranks fourth.

Ohio State dots its i. The Longhorns have their eyes of Texas.

Both have war chests bigger than a third world country.

This war of wills at Royal-Memorial Stadium on Saturday night is so highly anticipated and promises to be so entertaining that 60 minutes may not be enough. It may need an extra second or two just to draw out the fun even longer like some other Big Ten games.

Just look at how evenly matched these teams are, even though Ohio State is No. 1 and Texas nearby at No. 5.

Texas has a great quarterback. Ohio State has a great quarterback. OK, a greater quarterback since Julian Sayin has been more accurate than Manning.

This should be a classic battle of exceptional receivers. If Jeremiah Smith isn't the best wideout in the the nation, Cam Coleman might be. With apologies to Malachi Toney.

When I asked Coleman if this game is for bragging rights as to who is the best receiver in college football, the transfer from Auburn paused and finally said, "I just want to go out and play my game."

The programs boast two of the best and most scrutinized head coaches in the game with a couple of exceptions. Sarkisian still has to win the big one. Ryan Day was probably days away from getting fired after yet another loss to Michigan and had to win a national championship to save his job in the 2024 season. And he did.

These two are alike in so many ways but also different. Before winning a title, Day could beat everybody but his biggest rival, Michigan, with a 2-4 record. Sarkisian owns his biggest rivals - he's 7-1 against Oklahoma, Texas A&M and Arkansas the last four years - but can't win the shiniest trophy of them all.

They're two of the biggest brands in all of college football with some shared colorful history. Before this recent renewal of rivalries, the pair met in 2005 and 2006. Texas won on the road in Columbus the first year. Ohio State won on the road in Austin the following season. Texas won the national title in 2005. Ohio State almost won it in 2006 until it met up with the Florida Gators.

"This will be the most-watched regular season game, arguably of all time," Sarkisian said.

That's a mouthful. But there's a reason that College GameDay is coming to town for the fourth time in the past five years instead of coming last week for Texas State. Texas is expecting to break its attendance record of 105,215 that showed up for a loss to Georgia in 2024.

On the face, this one will be a game between two equals in terms of talent level. There's no telling how many NFL scouts and Lane Kiffin will be here to, uh, evaluate these players.

Heck, these two teams appear to be so even on paper that the betting line is just as close. Texas is a 1½-point favorite.

If they play on Saturday half as well as they talked on Monday, they cannot be beat.

It wasn't so much coach speak as much as it was no-speak. The Longhorns gave the Buckeyes their flowers and didn't utter a discouraging word.

Sarkisian and the seven players made available were so effusive in their loving compliments about Ohio State, you would have thought they were on the Buckeyes payroll. You might have come away from Monday's two-plus hours of conversations with the idea Texas was playing Rice this weekend.

But just know this. Arch Manning and the boys are excited.

articles.title: 35-year-old German footballer arrested over suspected revenge poisoning that killed team-mate
articles.summary: Football News: A shocking incident unfolds as a 35-year-old German amateur footballer is arrested for allegedly poisoning his team-mate during a trip, leading to his death. Investigations suggest a revenge motive linked to personal conflicts.
articles.body: A 35-year-old German amateur footballer has been arrested on suspicion of fatally poisoning his team-mate during an end-of-season trip, with prosecutors reportedly investigating whether the killing was an alleged act of revenge.The player, named as Marius, was arrested on Tuesday, September 1, after investigators came to suspect he had secretly administered poison to Philipp, 30, during a team trip to Dresden.Philipp became unwell during the trip involving players from amateur club TuS Rockenberg and grew seriously ill after returning home. His family called emergency services and he was taken to hospital, where he died the following day, June 16, 2025, despite attempts to resuscitate him.His cause of death was later established as septic multi-organ failure caused by poisoning, according to reports cited by NeedToKnow.Prosecutor suspects 'act of revenge'The circumstances initially appeared less sinister.According to reports, people close to Philipp initially believed he could have suffered severe food poisoning after the team ate fish during their trip to Dresden.Investigators later reached a different conclusion and identified Marius as a suspect in Philipp's death.Senior public prosecutor Thomas Hauburger told local media: “We assume that this was an act of revenge.”Rumours circulating in Rockenberg have reportedly suggested that the two footballers had been arguing over a woman, although that has not been established as the motive and remains part of the speculation surrounding the case.Marius is now in pre-trial detention and, according to the reports, has so far made no statement regarding the allegations.He has not been convicted of any offence in connection with Philipp's death, and neither he nor his legal representatives had publicly responded to the allegations at the time of reporting.The arrest has left those at TuS Rockenberg shocked, particularly given the circumstances surrounding Philipp's death.The club's head of football, Manuel Barufe, told local media: “We are all surprised and shocked.“Nobody expected this. We hope the police can fully clarify what happened.”TuS Rockenberg later released a statement on social media following Marius' arrest, saying the latest developments had left the club “speechless” after it had already been forced to deal with the sudden death of a team-mate the previous year.The club said: “After having to cope with the sudden death of a teammate in our football department last year, the events of last Tuesday have once again left us speechless.“None of us can currently comprehend this latest devastating blow. We are now placing our hopes in the work of the authorities and trust that the incident will be fully investigated.“Given the extremely distressing and emotional situation for everyone involved at our club, we will not comment on the ongoing investigation. We therefore urgently and respectfully ask that players, coaches and board members are not approached for comment.“Thank you for your understanding.”Philipp remembered as 'a man with a big heart'Following Philipp's death last year, TuS Rockenberg paid tribute to him, describing him as “a friend, a fighter on the pitch and a man with a big heart”.His family also remembered him for his personality, describing him as “the loud laughter, the quiet gestures and the big heart”.The latest development has come at a particularly striking point in Marius' personal life.According to reports, the accused footballer had already married in a civil ceremony after the alleged poisoning, but a much larger wedding celebration was due to take place this month, meaning his arrest came only around two weeks before the planned celebration.Marius remains in detention while the investigation into Philipp's death continues.The allegations against him remain unproven, with authorities yet to establish publicly whether the suspected poisoning was carried out as revenge or what precisely investigators believe happened during the team trip to Dresden.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Power outage leads to 100-minute delay ahead of No. 19 SMU and Florida State
articles.summary: The final game of Week 1 did not start on time.
articles.body:
The final game of Week 1 didn't start on time.

No. 19 SMU's game at Florida State was delayed after the power went out minutes before the scheduled kickoff time of just after 7:30 p.m. ET. The game finally began at 9:15 p.m. ET with partial lighting in the stadium and limited electronics.

The game clock was set to be kept on the field, players didn't have helmet communications and there would be no instant replay reviews because of the lack of power.

After what happened Saturday in Ann Arbor , that's an important point.

Per ESPN's broadcast, a transformer blew as the power was trying to be restored to the stadium. What initially hoped to be a very brief delay stretched over an hour.

The game is the first for the Mustangs in 2026, while FSU is already 1-0. The Seminoles played in Week Zero and beat New Mexico State 34-17. Florida State is off in Week 2, while SMU is scheduled to host FCS school UC Davis at 4 p.m. ET on Sept. 12.

articles.title: FSU vs. SMU Delayed with Power Outage, Check Out Photos, Videos of Doak Campbell Stadium
articles.summary: Florida State and SMU will have to wait a bit longer than expected to start their game on Monday.
articles.body:
Florida State and SMU will have to wait a bit longer than expected to start their game on Monday.

The game between the Seminoles and Mustangs was delayed because of a power outage at Doak Campbell Stadium. Kickoff was initially set for 7:30 p.m. ET, but Florida State announced that there would be an update at 8:20, followed by a 10-minute warm-up period.

Watch: CFB QB's face bloodied after facemask penalty

The game was then delayed until at least 9:15, although with significant restrictions.

The blackout led to some jarring images during the waiting period:

ESPN's Taylor McGregor provided several updates during the delay, nothing the game could have been played on Tuesday:

According to The Athletic's David Ubben , the teams were making their entrances ahead of kickoff when the stadium lights flashed and then went out across the stadium.

Minutes later, the stadium screens displayed a message saying that the game had been delayed because of a power outage.

ESPN's Taylor McGregor said on the broadcast that Florida State attempted to reset the stadium's power, and a transformer blew out. There was also a power outage on campus overnight.

The No. 19 Mustangs come into the game as a 2.5-point favorite over the Seminoles, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Florida State started its season with a Week 0 victory over New Mexico State.

The Seminoles have a tough start to the season, facing SMU this week before taking on No. 13 Alabama on the road next week. Florida State is looking to return to national relevance, and a few wins over ranked opponents would help set the tone.

The Mustangs reached the College Football Playoff two years ago but went 9-4 last year. After facing Florida State this week, they'll take on UC Davis next week.

articles.title: Miami, More CFB Teams Troll Florida State During Blackout in Viral Social Media Post
articles.summary: Miami used Florida State's power outage as an opportunity to troll their in-state rival.
articles.body:
Miami used Florida State's power outage as an opportunity to troll their in-state rival.

The Hurricanes made a post letting fans know they won't have to deal with a lengthy delay ahead of their game against Florida A&M on Thursday.

Baylor, TCU and Virginia piled on as well.

Florida State and SMU were set to kick things off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Monday, but the game was delayed nearly two hours because of a power outage before finally getting underway.

The Hurricanes will face the Seminoles in October, and Florida State will look to get back at them for the troll job on Monday.

articles.title: Is Champions League three-peat really possible for PSG?
articles.summary: Luis Enrique's Paris Saint-Germain have already secured their status as one of the Champions League's greatest teams by winning the trophy in back-to-back ye...
articles.body:
Luis Enrique's Paris Saint-Germain have already secured their status as one of the Champions League's greatest teams by winning the trophy in back-to-back years, and now they have their sights set on a rare treble.

"Doing the treble is the objective, but we know it's going to be very difficult and that there will be obstacles in our way," said PSG captain Marquinhos on the eve of the campaign.

After years of disappointment in Europe for the Qatar-owned club, PSG became the real deal after former Barcelona and Spain coach Luis Enrique was appointed in 2023.

They reached the semi-finals in his first season, then kicked on following the departure of Kylian Mbappe in 2024.

No longer beholden to one or two superstar names, PSG went on to blow the rest of Europe away en route to winning a first Champions League title in 2025 as they destroyed Inter Milan 5-0 in the final.

They followed that up by edging Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties in last season's final in Budapest, becoming just the second side to retain the trophy since the inception of the modern Champions League in 1992.

But a three-peat at this level would be an achievement on another scale again.

Real Madrid did it under Zinedine Zidane, reigning over the continent from 2016 to 2018.

Johan Cruyff's Ajax and Franz Beckenbauer's Bayern Munich both won three successive European Cups in the 1970s, while Alfredo Di Stefano's Madrid won five on the bounce at the dawn of the competition between 1956 and 1960.

That is the kind of exalted company PSG are hoping to join, but the demands in Europe's elite club competition are now greater than ever -- the new Champions League format led to the Parisians playing a total of 17 games in order to win the trophy in each of the last two campaigns.

When at their best, they are utterly thrilling. Their pace in an attack led by Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is utterly terrifying, and is supported by flying full-backs Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes.

Meanwhile their midfield three, led by diminutive Portuguese playmaker Vitinha, can dominate games against far more physical opponents.

Hence PSG winning their two titles, and two UEFA Super Cups, despite playing 18 matches against Premier League teams in the last two years.

The number of games might be the biggest danger for PSG, who played 121 competitive matches across the last two seasons with a meagre three-week break in between because of the Club World Cup.

Either side of that, the majority of their squad were involved in major tournaments in 2024 and have had another shortened summer holiday due to the World Cup.

That may explain why they have looked rusty at the beginning of this campaign. However, their margin over the rest of France's top flight is so great that they are still favourites to win Ligue 1 again, even if they choose to regularly rest key players to keep them fresh for the Champions League.

Their European campaign could not start with a kinder fixture either, with Slovan Bratislava up first -- things will quickly move up a notch, though, as they visit Manchester City and host Barcelona in October.

PSG do not often sell one of their star players but that is what they have done with Bradley Barcola, who joined Liverpool for huge money. Goncalo Ramos, Lee Kang-in and Ibrahim Mbaye, all useful squad options last season, have been sold too.

However, Maghnes Akliouche, who played for France at the World Cup, and Ferran Torres -- Spain's final match-winner in North America -- are headline new arrivals. The latter played under Luis Enrique for his country.

"He was like a footballing father for me when I played for him in the national team," Torres said after signing from Barcelona.

Luis Enrique is the star now, more than any individual player, and he has just signed a new contract to stay in Paris until 2030.

"It is the first time I have stayed four years at the same club, and I am more motivated than I was in my first year," he said, insisting that he has lost none of his hunger. That is ominous for PSG's rivals.

articles.title: The best and worst of Week 1 in the American Conference
articles.summary: Tulsa’s defense pulled off a signature upset for the American. But Charlotte showed significant concern.
articles.body:
All 14 American Conference teams have now taken the field in the 2026 season. Eight of the 14 teams secured a victory in Week 1, with Memphis improving to a conference-best 2-0 after starting its season in Week 0.

Here are the best and worst things that happened in the American in Week 1 of the new 2026 season:

Tulsa ended its 10-game drought against Oklahoma State last September, storming into Stillwater and ousting the Cowboys, 19-12. Despite receiving homefield advantage in the rematch, the difficulty of the matchup significantly ramped up this year. Oklahoma State hired Eric Morris, who directed the nation's No. 1 scoring offense at 45.1 points per game in 2025. Morris also brought along the FBS leading passer Drew Mestemaker, fifth-leading rusher Caleb Hawkins, and third-leading receiver Wyatt Young.

With an FBS record 91 newcomers, the Cowboys were slated to drastically improved upon their 134th-ranked scoring offense from 2025. But Tulsa's defense begged to differ.

The Golden Hurricane stifled Mestemaker and the Cowboys to a mere 10 points in a 24-10 victory. Oklahoma State's revamped offense scored fewer points Saturday than it did last September against Tulsa. While the Golden Hurricane won the turnover battle 4-1, the Golden Hurricane didn't even need a significant turnover advantage to win — with two takeaways coming in the final 4:30 of action in a 14-point ballgame.

Tulsa's veteran secondary led by free safety Zach Williams held Mestemaker to 241 passing yards on a 29-of-49 showing. Inside linebacker Chris Thompson Jr. spearheaded the run defense with 10 tackles and generated a tone-setting red zone stop on Oklahoma State's opening possession. Tulsa created constant pressure throughout the matchup as Oklahoma State never recovered from losing offensive tackle Jacob Sexton in the first quarter.

Charlotte finished 1-11 last season. The 49ers defeated one FCS opponent, Monmouth, by seven on a go-ahead touchdown in the final two minutes. All 11 of their losses were by double-digits.

What if I told you things actually got worse for Charlotte in 2026?

Charlotte was one of three FBS victims that dropped their opener to FCS competition, falling 43-41 to The Citadel in triple overtime. And The Citadel isn't exactly the next North Dakota State, as it dropped its opener to Wofford, 42-14, on Aug. 29. Charlotte posted 538 yards on the FCS foe but committed two costly turnovers in the first half, which kept The Citadel in the gamer.

The 49ers played from behind toward the end of regulation, needing a tying touchdown with 24 seconds remaining to send the game to overtime. Upon reaching OT, Charlotte had several disasters. The 49ers displayed one of the worst tackling attempts of the week to give The Citadel a 25-yard touchdown in first overtime.

And during the 2-point shootout in third overtime, Charlotte quarterback Cole Gonzales overthrew an open Jaylen Hampton in the end zone, leading to a stunning upset.

Charlotte now rides a 10-game losing streak. It plays at Ole Miss next week.

The best: Jaylin Carter and the Memphis crowd

Jaylin Carter is the current FBS rushing leader. Yes, he has an advantage over most of the country considering Memphis was one of 16 teams to play in Week 0. After producing a 36-yard breakaway touchdown in the opener at UNLV, the Southern Miss only added to an impressive early season résumé against Arkansas State.

Carter posted 183 rushing yards in a 42-24 victory and tied a school record by producing four rushing touchdowns. He broke free for a 74-yard touchdown scamper in the third quarter and put on the finishing efforts in the fourth with a 24-yard sealing score. Carter produced 110 yards in the second half alone as Memphis won its sixth-straight matchup over the Red Wolves. Marcus Stokes compared Carter's running style to that of Le'Veon Bell in the postgame press conference.

Additionally, Carter did it all in front of one of the most electrifying crowds the American Conference has seen in a while. Charles Huff called Tiger fans to pack Liberty Stadium, and they responded with 45,632. It marked the stadium's crowd for a Memphis game since the 2023 Liberty Bowl vs. Iowa State. For a regular season game, it was Memphis' greatest crowd since hosting College GameDay vs. SMU in 2019.

The worst: South Florida's offensive showing

South Florida was one of five FBS programs to average over 40 points per game in 2025. The Bulls were home to the nation's third-ranked offense at 488 per game, showing a tremendous balance between the run and pass in Alex Golesh's "go-go-go" up-tempo scheme. However, Golesh left for Auburn, as did quarterback Byrum Brown, and a slew of the team's top receivers.

South Florida only retained one offensive starter from 2025 in guard Thomas Shrader. Under the direction of new head coach Brian Hartline, who previously served as Ohio State's offensive coordinator, the Bulls showed some growing pains with the retooled group. USF started 1-0, but the 19-9 victory over FIU could have been much more aesthetically pleasing.

USF only generated 208 yards of offense compared to FIU's 308, and the Bulls were limited to 100 in the passing game led by quarterback Michael Van Buren Jr. And if not for frequent FIU mistakes, such as the Panthers' three turnovers and eight penalties, the Bulls might have been upset at home. South Florida never had a single offensive play generate more than 14 yards. The Bulls scored 13 of their 16 points in the fourth quarter, but all three of those scoring drives were off turnovers and required 35 yards or fewer.

South Florida never had a single drive span more than 39 yards in the opener, which must be improved immediately as conference play starts Saturday at Army.

The American Conference features three option-based offenses: Army, Navy, and Rice. All three teams dominated FCS competition in Week 1. Army handled Bryant, 59-3. Navy annihilated Towson, 42-15. And Rice flew past Houston Christian, 31-3. And all three teams ran the dang ball.

Army involved 16 different ball carriers, which produced 569 yards and 10 touchdowns on 57 carries, nearly averaging a first down per attempt. It marked the most rushing yards by an FBS team since 2022. Quarterback Cale Hellums and slotback Zach Mundell led the charge in a concerted effort, combining for 192 yards and four touchdowns in the victory. Army's passing stats? 7-of-13 for 79 yards. Just run the dang ball.

Navy also eclipsed the half-millennium mark, recording 506 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 73 attempts. Quarterback Braxton Woodson, taking the reins from program legend Blake Horvath, fulfilled his new role nicely, in a 200-yard explosion. He was one of two 200-yard rushers in Week 1, sharing the honors with Duke running back Nate Sheppard. Navy's passing stats? 3-of-6 for 21 yards. Just run the dang ball.

Rice is newer to the option game, implementing the scheme last season under head coach Scott Abell. Rice managed 465 rushing yards, its most since 2004, and four touchdowns in its 2026 opener. Sophomore running back Tyvonn Byars eclipsed the century mark for the first time in a 104-yard masterclass, while new quarterback Jacurri Brown added 98. Rice's passing stats? 4-of-10 for 28 yards. Just run the dang ball.

Tulane is the standard of the American Conference. You earn that title after securing four consecutive American Conference Championship Game berths and two championships over that timeframe, plus a 2022 Cotton Bowl victory and 2025 College Football Playoff appearance.

But the Green Wave proved there's plenty of work to be done to extend that streak or qualify for a second-straight CFP appearance. Tulane debuted new head coach Will Hall, who previously served as the program's offensive coordinator in 2019-20 and passing game coordinator in 2025. Hall's debut could have gone much better.

Tulane was held entirely out of the end zone for the first time since 2019 in the 17-3 defeat at Duke. The Green Wave committed 15 penalties — the most in all of Week 1 — for 104 yards. The ground defense, which was strength in 2025, turned into a weakness as Duke running back Nate Sheppard gashed Tulane with 227 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

Meanwhile, Tulane couldn't establish anything on the ground in a 54-yard rushing performance. The Green Wave tried both Zeon Chriss-Gremillion and Kadin Semonza at quarterback but never found the end zone with either. They never took a snap inside the Duke 19-yard line in a severe offensive struggle. Nobody's a finished product in Week 1, but Tulane's CFP aspirations took a significant hit — considering the Green Wave's win over Duke essentially got them in last year.

UTSA handled second-year FCS startup UTRGV in the Alamodome, 45-16, and the Roadrunners saw exactly what they needed to see on offense. Owen McCown threw for 275 yards and three touchdowns on a 22-of-27 showing. Will Henderson III recorded rushing 101 yards and A'Marion Peterson nearly reached triple-digits, spotting him with a 98-yard performance.

UTSA logged 527 yards of offense in the opener, and the most impressive were the seven belonging to tight end Brandon Young Jr. In the early second quarter, Young got the Alamodome on its feet with a SportsCenter Top 10 highlight grab in the end zone.

articles.title: El Madrid inicia la defensa del título... a la caza del Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El juvenil madridista, vigente campeón de la Youth, debuta ante el Inter con el objetivo de cazar a los azulgrana en el palmarés de la competición
articles.summary: El juvenil madridista, vigente campeón de la Youth, debuta ante el Inter con el objetivo de cazar a los azulgrana en el palmarés de la competición
articles.body: El Juvenil A del Real Madrid comienza hoy la defensa del trono europeo, en el que se sentó el pasado 20 de abril tras conquistar la segunda Youth League de su historia. El vigente campeón de la Champions juvenil arranca ante el Inter en el Di Stéfano (16.00 horas, RMTV) el camino para revalidar un título con el que cazaría al Barcelona en el palmarés de la Youth League. Los azulgrana mandan hasta el momento con tres títulos en sus vitrinas, pero el Madrid ya le pisa los talones con dos. Además, de volver a ganar la Youth se convertirían en el segundo equipo tras el Chelsea que logra dos títulos consecutivas. Son los dos premios extra que le esperan el Real Madrid por defender la corona continental juvenil. No sólo el equipo haría historia. También su entrenador, Álvaro López, que se convertiría en el segundo entrenador en lograr dos títulos de la Youth League tras Adi Viveash, que lo consiguió al frente del Chelsea. El técnico madridista fue la gran sensación en los banquillos de La Fábrica la pasada temporada. Tras coger al Juvenil A a mitad de temporada, lo llevó a un histórico triplete ganando Youth League, Liga y Copa de Campeones. Ahora busca el más difícil todavía, con cinco títulos en juego. El Madrid inicia el asalto a la nueva Youth League con un equipo en el que apenas quedan un puñado de los héroes juveniles que conquistaron el título la pasada temporada. De los 25 jugadores convocados para la Final Four del pasado mes de abril, sólo siete repetirán a las órdenes de Álvaro López en el estreno de la presente edición ante el Inter: Lacosta, Adri Pérez, Lezcano, Ciria, Joan, Yáñez y Carlos Díez. Los tres últimos ocupando los tres cupos por convocatoria de jugadores nacidos en 2007 (ya no son juveniles) que se pueden utilizar. El Juvenil A del Real Madrid se presenta al estreno europeo ante el Inter después de debutar el pasado sábado con victoria en Liga, ganando 3-0 al Rayo Majadahonda. Un triunfo de mérito porque Álvaro López afrontó el partido con numerosas bajas y muchas de ellas las arrastrará en la Youth. El técnico no podrá contar por lesión con Enzo Alves, Lemaitre, Mauro Bautista, Manu Romero y Rubén López, además de Bugarín y Álex Mora, en plantilla del Juvenil B pero en la órbita del primer juvenil.

articles.title: Lille - Betis: Volver... que 20 años no es nada
articles.standfirst: Los verdiblancos regresan a la Champions League más de dos décadas después
articles.summary: Los verdiblancos regresan a la Champions League más de dos décadas después
articles.body: En 1934, Carlos Gardel y Alfredo Le Pera compusieron Volver, uno de los tangos más famosos de la historia y de la música argentina. En su letra, la nostalgia por el paso del tiempo queda reflejada en una frase, “que veinte años no es nada”, una afirmación que ha trascendido hasta emplearse de manera habitual en el lenguaje popular. Aunque para el Betis, que tras veinte años, nueve meses y dos días de su última aparición regresa hoy a la Champions League, la máxima competición de clubes del fútbol europeo, sí ha sido mucho tiempo. Tal vez demasiado. Desde la última vez que sonó la música, un 6 de diciembre de 2005 con una derrota en casa frente al Anderlecht, los verdiblancos han sufrido mil contratiempos: dos descensos, una intervención judicial con un concurso de acreedores, problemas económicos y societarios, el trágico fallecimiento del eterno Miki Roqué... Pero con la fuerza de una afición inquebrantable han sabido levantarse con dos ascensos, una histórica Junta de Accionistas en la que lograron terminar con una época de sombras, varios regresos a Europa, un título de Copa... Un camino repleto de baches hasta llegar aquí, al Estadio Pierre-Mauroy, actual Decathlon Arena, en el que arranca una nueva aventura en la máxima competición continental. El conjunto verdiblanco aprovechó la plaza extra para el torneo otorgada por la UEFA a España, fruto de los buenos resultados en Europa de sus equipos, para acceder, como quinto clasificado de LaLiga, a una Champions que medirá el proceso de crecimiento que el club ha experimentado en la última década. El Lille de Davide Ancelotti será el primer escollo de una fase de liga en la que clubes como el Bayern Munich, el Arsenal, el Oporto o el Borussia Dortmund, entre otros, se cruzarán también en su camino. Los del hijo de Carletto llegan en un gran momento de resultados, invictos en el arranque de la Ligue 1, y después de imponerse el pasado jueves al Toulouse por 0-1 con un gol del japonés Ayase Ueda, estableciendo un récord histórico de ocho victorias consecutivas a domicilio en el campeonato francés. Pero también demostraron su capacidad para sufrir: su rival remató 24 veces y el guardameta Berke Özer tuvo que intervenir en nueve ocasiones. Con experiencia europea reciente, el respaldo de su afición y un equipo en el que aparecen nombres como el incombustible Olivier Giroud, el exbético Perraud o el hermano pequeño de Kylian Mbappé, Ethan, el conjunto francés será la primera piedra de toque para un Betis que aterriza en el país vecino con la práctica totalidad de su plantilla disponible, más de 800 aficionados acompañándolo y la ilusión de volver a estar por fin entre los mejores. De sus titulares habituales, sólo se quedó en Sevilla el marroquí Abde, con molestias en una rodilla. Pero el potencial verdiblanco queda reflejado en las 11 Champions ganadas entre Isco (cinco), Ceballos (tres), Bartra (dos) y Fran García (una) o los más de 250 partidos disputados en la competición entre los integrantes del plantel. También por Pellegrini, con 72 duelos y que llevó al Villarreal y el City a semifinales, y al Málaga a cuartos. Pero para el Ingeniero, aunque hoy sea el día de un soñado regreso tras 20 años de ausencia, la Liga sigue siendo prioridad y estudia rotaciones... El Betis sueña en grande y espera no tener que esperar tanto tiempo para volver.

articles.summary: "Los que me quieren lo harán siempre y los que no, aunque gane la Bota de Oro, van a seguir sin hacerlo"
articles.body: Álvaro Morata, fichaje estrella del Leganés tras llegar a Butarque cedido por el Como, explica en el programa 'El Larguero' de la Cadena SER su decisión de fichar por un equipo de LaLiga HyperMotion a pesar de tener importantes ofertas de Europa. "Muy contento, al final creo que es un proyecto fantástico, con una apuesta muy fuerte desde el club y la propiedad. Es un proyecto con muy buena pinta y desde que firmé yo aquí, hay muchos jugadores que se han interesado por el club y que me preguntan. Yo tampoco me esperaba esta repercusión mediática. Es un club que me encanta como está haciendo las cosas, la gente que trabaja y el ambiente que se respira en el estadio", le reconoció el delantero de 33 años a Manu Carreño. A la pregunta de si "¿vienes al Leganés sólo por jugar en Madrid?" destacó que "está claro que no. Es un decisión tomada en base a un proyecto muy ilusionante, que me gusta y que creo que va a hacer muy bien las cosas". Morata quiso destacar que "en el Como fui mucho más importante de lo que se dice" y que "siempre pienso en hacer a mis compañeros mejores y creo que eso es bueno". Respecto a sus primeras experiencias con la camiseta del Leganés el ex de Atlético de Madrid y Real Madrid compartió que "llegué a casa y me di cuenta de que hacía tiempo que no disfrutaba tanto". "He pasado unos años complicados, pero ahora estoy feliz y creo que eso se nota. Hasta disfruté de un viaje, camino a Canarias, que hace unos años me habrían dado mucha más pereza. Simplemente es disfrutar de las cosas cotidianas", declaró. Morata reconoce que "lo que hayas hecho hasta aquí no vale de nada cuando te pones la camiseta del Leganés. El otro día estaba como si fuera el primer día de mi carrera". "Me he dado cuenta de que mi historia no la voy a cambiar. En vez de venir al Leganés, tuve una oferta de un entrenador con el que tengo buena relación y que jugaba competición europea. Y meter 20 ó 30 goles no me iba a cambiar la vida, pero igual subir a Primera con este equipo sí. Es un reto diferente. Las personas que me quieran me van a querer siempre y a las que no les guste, por mucho que gane la Bota de Oro, van a seguir sin hacerlo. He cambiado el Leganés por algún proyecto de Champions, sí. Pero mi Champions es tomar una decisión que yo considero valiente. No quiero que parezca que estoy aquí sólo por estar en casa. Estoy aquí por el proyecto que tienen y porque espero quedarme. Y porque ellos me han demostrado que me quieren aquí", reflexionó. Álvaro Morata comentó la rueda de prensa Jose Mourinho tras la derrota del Real Madrid contra el Real Betis: "¿Quieres que diga la verdad? Yo no veía la hora de que dijera alguna así porque a mí me divierte. A mí, como aficionado, quiero decir. Ojalá que el Atlético gane la liga, pero si hay un Clásico yo lo voy a ver también por verle a él. Aporta al espectáculo". Álvaro Morata, que ha sido 87 veces internacional con España, compartió sus sensaciones y emociones tras ver al equipo de Luis de la Fuente ganar el Mundial 2026. "Me habría flipado estar en el Mundial. Pero fui a Nueva York casi sintiéndome parte, por ver a muchos jugadores que empezaron a ir a la Selección conmigo. Puedes pensar qué habría pasado si el año hubiera sido diferente, pero no vale de nada. Yo lo tenía claro antes de que Luis de la Fuente diera la lista. Somos personas y al final una parte de ti tiene ilusión de que te lleve, siempre hay esperanza. Y creo que podría aportar al grupo, para hacer buena dinámica, pero también para el míster iba a ser más fácil si yo no estaba. Imagínate, arrancas un Mundial y empieza a decir todo el mundo que qué pinto yo allí. Mejor evitar ese ruido. Y Borja y el resto de delanteros también lo merecían. Lo del nivel de Oyarzabal yo siempre lo he dicho, igual que lo de Ferran. Metió el gol que me habría gustado meter a mí y me alegré muchísimo por él", declaró. Morata recordó que "sí, me llamó De la Fuente para decirme que no iba. Creo que fue incluso antes de la prelista. Yo se lo agradecí, le dije que lo entendía perfectamente y les deseé toda la suerte del mundo. Lo único que no cumplió su promesa conmigo, porque me dijo que si era campeón iba a salir a caballo con la Copa en la mano... Igual todavía está a tiempo (risas). Los chavales lo han cumplido, que Cucurella tiene ahí su tatuaje". El nuevo delantero del Leganés dijo, sobre su futuro en la Selección, que no "yo no cierro la puerta, claro que me gustaría volver". "Pero hay que ser honestos y ahora mismo es una locura. Lo veo muy difícil por la competencia que hay. Lo hablaba el otro día en el vestuario, estamos en un momento fantástico de la posición del '9' con Espí, Gonzalo, Chupe, Arnau, Samu... Más los que ya están. Creo que España tiene el mejor nivel en todas las posiciones desde hace tiempo", reconoció.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund - Villarreal | Un muro para disipar las dudas
articles.standfirst: Tras un mal comienzo en Liga, el submarino regresa a la máxima competición continental en el escenario donde recibió la peor goleada de la temporada pasada
articles.summary: Tras un mal comienzo en Liga, el submarino regresa a la máxima competición continental en el escenario donde recibió la peor goleada de la temporada pasada
articles.body: Que todo cambio de ciclo exige un proceso y suele implicar un peaje en forma de puntos perdidos era algo asumido en el Villarreal cuando decidió cerrar la etapa de Marcelino para abrir la de Iñigo Pérez. Sin embargo, eso no evita que el inicio de temporada esté siendo más duro de lo esperado en la entidad azulejera. “El arranque es muy malo, no hay que ponerle pomada: es irritante, es amargo, tenemos dolor”, reconoció el técnico tras la derrota del pasado sábado ante el Dépor. Con este clima de incertidumbre llega el Villarreal a Dortmund para su debut en la Champions. Ni el estado de ánimo es el ideal ni el Signal Iduna Park parece el escenario más propicio para cambiar la dinámica. Además, en la memoria sigue muy presente el 4-0 encajado la pasada temporada en su visita al conjunto alemán. Pero las grandes reacciones necesitan un golpe de efecto, y pocos más impactantes podrían darse ahora mismo que derribar el famoso muro amarillo para iniciar la remontada. El Villarreal regresa a la Liga de Campeones y lo hace, por primera vez en su historia, por segunda temporada consecutiva. La pasada campaña, sin embargo, el sueño europeo acabó en pesadilla: el submarino solo sumó un punto y terminó como el segundo peor equipo del torneo. Un fracaso impropio que empañó una temporada sobresaliente en LaLiga y dejó un inevitable sabor amargo. El objetivo de los de Iñigo Pérez pasa por ofrecer una imagen mucho más competitiva y pelear por la clasificación. Sin embargo, el calendario es incluso más exigente que el del pasado curso. Dortmund será la primera parada de un recorrido en el que también aparecen Liverpool, PSG, United o Nápoles. Ganar los partidos más asequibles, como los ante Slavia de Praga y Sabah, y firmar un par de grandes resultados parece casi obligatorio. En Alemania deberán intentar lograr el primero. Los amarillos llegan al coliseo germano con dudas en defensa, tanto por las bajas como por el pobre rendimiento mostrado hasta ahora. Juan Foyth no llegará a tiempo, mientras que Carlos Romero, ausente la pasada jornada por problemas físicos, apunta de nuevo a quedarse fuera. El técnico navarro deberá decidir entre mantener a Logan Costa junto a Renato Veiga o dar entrada a un inédito Pau Navarro, el defensa más destacado del equipo la temporada pasada. Donde sí parece avecinarse un relevo es en la portería. Mantener a Luiz Junior resulta complicado de justificar tras un inicio de curso en el que ha quedado señalado en varios encuentros. El sábado incluso escuchó pitos de la grada tras encajar otro gol evitable. Todo apunta a que llegará la hora de Gulacsi, veterano guardameta curtido en mil batallas y habituado a escenarios como el de Dortmund tras sus numerosas visitas con el Leipzig. Por su parte, el Dortmund afronta el partido con la tranquilidad de haber arrancado la Bundesliga con dos victorias y haber recuperado su fiabilidad tras remontar dos goles ante el Hoffenheim el sábado.

articles.title: Maresca arranca donde lo dejó Pep
articles.standfirst: El Manchester City arranca una nueva era en Europa
articles.summary: El Manchester City arranca una nueva era en Europa
articles.body: La 'era Maresca' no ha arrancado mal en Mánchester. Si bien perdieron la Supercopa ante el Arsenal, han sumado tres triunfos en los tres primeros partidos de la Premier y son, junto a los 'Gunners', líderes del campeonato inglés. Ahora, y mientras de reojo miran al derbi ante el Manchester United del próximo domingo, los 'sky blues' se estrenan en Champions con la alargada sombra de Guardiola todavía sobre el nuevo proyecto del que ha sido el gran dominador del fútbol inglés en la última década. El gran objetivo se alcanzó en 2023, cuando ante el Inter cosecharon la primera y única Champions en la historia del club. Ahora, con movimientos como el de Enzo Fernández, Ndiaye, Elliot Anderson o Bouaddi dejan claro que con una en el museo no es suficiente. Quieren más. Para Maresca será su segunda Champions League como entrenador. Quizás, la primera completa. Debutó en la pasada 2025-26 con el Chelsea pero apenas dirigió seis encuentros. Fue despedido antes de acabar la fase liga y no estuvo en los octavos, cuando el Chelsea perdió ante el PSG. Su rival será un compatriota: Francesco Farioli. Otro joven entrenador italiano que tuvo que salir del país para crecer como técnico. El que fuera asistente de De Zerbi hizo campeón al Oporto el curso pasado y ha devuelto a los 'Dragones' a la Champions League Ser campeón de Europa League y repetir clasificación a Champions no fue suficiente para evitar un verano de miedo en Birmingham. El Aston Villa perdió a Watkins, Rogers, Tielemans, Konsa, Digne o el 'Dibu' Martínez... y ha arrancado la Premier con apenas un punto en tres jornadas. Para iniciar su participación en Champions visitan al siempre complicado Brujas, un clásico de esta competición.

articles.title: Real Madrid vs Inter: Champions League – preview, team news, prediction
articles.summary: Mourinho kicks off the record 15-time Champions League winners’ European campaign against Serie A champions Inter.
articles.body:
Who: Real Madrid vs Inter Milan What: Champions League league phase Where: Santiago Bernabeu, Madrid, Spain When: Tuesday, September 8, at 9pm (19:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

When Jose Mourinho left Inter Milan for Real Madrid in the summer of 2010, after leading the Italian outfit to Champions League glory, he was at the peak of his powers.

The Portuguese coach claimed an historic treble with Inter, clinching Serie A in the last week of the season and lifting the Coppa Italia.

Inter beat Bayern 2-0 in the Champions League final at Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu stadium, winning the trophy for the first time since 1965 and becoming the first Italian team to win the treble.

The day after the final Mourinho said it was likely his last match in charge and about a week later his appointment at Real Madrid was finalised.

Now 16 years on, and beginning his second stint at Madrid, Mourinho kicks off the record 15-time Champions League winners’ European campaign against Serie A champions Inter on Tuesday at the Bernabeu.

Mourinho denies feeling pressure to lift Champions League

The Champions League is the only trophy that evaded Mourinho during his first stint at Real Madrid.

“No, it is two different spells,” he said when asked at a pre-match news conference if he was in debt to the club. “When I left in 2013, we won what we won and lost what we lost and ‌we gave it our all. And that was that. What I need to do now has nothing to do with the past.”

“Back in 2010, we weren’t even reaching the quarterfinals of the Champions League and it had been ages since we’d played in a semifinal. Now we’ve won six Champions Leagues in a little over a decade.”

All eyes will be on how Real respond to their first setback of Mourinho’s second spell – a 1-0 defeat ⁠by Real Betis in La Liga on Friday.

“We want to win every ⁠match, every competition,” he said. But you have to work to accomplish stability. Stability. Stability … Structure …

“So Real Madrid need to reach that stability that is so important to achieve something great. But Real Madrid are Real Madrid, you ⁠need to win here no matter what.”

Sitting alongside Mourinho, star striker Kylian Mbappe was asked several times about his relationship ⁠with Vinicius Jr and the atmosphere in the Real dressing room.

“What does an improvement in the dressing room mean?” Mbappe said when asked if there had been a change from last year.

“Do you have the feeling that something wasn’t right ‌last year? No, it’s the same as last year. It’s true we have a different coach, but it’s the same.”

Mbappe acknowledged his side have to improve in front of goal.

“I could say that I score more goals than some PSG players so they need to score more, but I have to be smart and acknowledge that I need to improve too, even if I do certain things that others don’t,” he said.

“It’s an endless debate. We all need to improve [in front of goal], and also with the ball.”

Mbappe missed a late penalty as Troy Parrott scored his first goal for Real Betis in their 1-0 win on Friday, ending Mourinho’s perfect start to the La Liga season.

Madrid had won each of their first three matches under Mourinho in his second spell in charge, but Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles denied Mbappe from the spot deep into stoppage time to seal a memorable victory at La Cartuja.

Vinicius Junior hit the post in the first half from Arda Guler’s pass across the face of goal, with Mbappe foiled twice by heroic blocks from Natan Bernardo de Souza and Marc Bartra.

As Madrid struggled to break Betis down, the hosts took a surprise lead nine minutes from time when Parrott fired home the rebound after Thibaut Courtois had produced a fine save to deny Nelson Deossa’s header.

A last-gasp winner from Lautaro Martinez sealed a breathless win for Inter as the Serie A champions fought back from two goals down to edge visiting Napoli 3-2 on Saturday.

The game exploded in the second half when Matteo Politano guided home a shot in the 50th minute before Rasmus Hojlund’s curler doubled the Napoli lead three minutes later.

Inter responded almost immediately when Martinez hammered in his first goal of the season from a Dimarco cross. Substitute Marcus Thuram came agonisingly close to a leveller when he headed off the post.

The France international would not be denied twice, though, and smashed a towering header past Alex Meret in the 82nd minute to level the scores.

Chances fell at both ends before Martinez’s penalty box instincts proved decisive in the 91st minute as Napoli failed to clear in a goalmouth scramble and the Argentina striker pounced to settle an extraordinary match.

The Opta supercomputer makes Real Madrid the favourites, with a win probability of 56 percent. Inter given a 22.3 percent chance of winning.

They have faced each other on 19 occasions; Madrid won 10 games, Inter won seven, and two ended as draws.

Somewhat surprisingly, Inter have not beaten Real Madrid since 1998, a game in which the great Roberto Baggio scored a brace for the Italians.

December 07, 2021: Real Madrid 2-0 Inter Milan (Champions League)

September 15, 2021: Inter Milan 0-1 Real Madrid (Champions League)

November 25, 2020: Inter Milan 0-2 Real Madrid (Champions League)

November 03, 2020: Real Madrid 3-2 Inter Milan (Champions League)

November 25, 1998: Inter Milan 3-1 Real Madrid (Champions League)

Eduardo Camavinga, Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva will all miss the game due to suspensions carried over from last season.

Madrid also have a host of injuries to contend with as Eder Militao, Rodrygo, Ferland Mendy and Raul Asencio are all ruled out.

Aurelien Tchouameni, Thiago Pitarch, Endrick and Marc Cucurella face late fitness tests as they struggle to recover from injuries, but all are reportedly back in training.

Left-back Federico Dimarco is unavailable due to a knee injury, while new signing Djed Spence is still working his way back to full fitness after an undisclosed injury and is unlikely to feature.

articles.title: Atlético, una obsesión ‘’especial’
articles.standfirst: Arranca una nueva Champions en Liverpool con el aliciente de que la final se disputa en el Metropolitano.
articles.summary: Arranca una nueva Champions en Liverpool con el aliciente de que la final se disputa en el Metropolitano.
articles.body: La élite del planeta fútbol tiene una fecha marcada en rojo: 5 de junio del 2027. También, un estadio: El Metropolitano. Una cita: la final de la Champions. Un gran premio: una orejona que, en muchos casos, es una auténtica obsesión. Y este es el caso del Atlético de Madrid de Simeone. Con el argentino al mando, los rojiblancos llegan tras ser el equipo español que más lejos llegó en la pasada edición. Tocó las semifinales en las que el Arsenal le apeó de la gran cita de Budapest por apenas un gol y busca este curso llegar a la cita definitiva, algo que ya hizo en 2014 y 2016 (en la era Cholista) y antes en 1974. Disputar la gran final en el Metropolitano es un acicate más para un equipo que posiblemente no necesite más en su búsqueda de la que sería su primera Champions. El intento llega en la decimocuarta participación seguida en la competición desde que Simeone tomó el mando para convertir en algo cotidiano, jugar entre los mejores, lo que era especial (desde el 78 hasta la llegada de Simeone en 2011 apenas se participó en cuatro ediciones del máximo torneo continental). Madrid, Barça, Bayern, PSG y Manchester City son los únicos cinco equipos que han acompañado sin fallo al Atlético durante todas estas ediciones. Un ejemplo del indiscutible y vital salto dado por el club del Metropolitano en estos tres lustros guiados por El Cholo. Además del argentino, el único que ha estado en todas y cada una de estas Champions ha sido Koke. Hasta hace apenas unos días, Giménez podía presumir también de formar parte de una plantilla que ahora ya dejó atrás para marcharse cedido al Deportivo. No es, en cualquier caso, Liverpool un escenario sencillo para emprender este camino a la Primera. Ya el año pasado empezó allí y fue con derrota en el tiempo añadido tras levantar un 2-0 con doblete de Llorente. Como el curso pasado, el inicio rojiblanco pasa por los rivales de más dificultad (visitan el Metropolitano Mánchester United y Bayern), principales escollos para lograr, en esta edición especial, meterse entre los ocho primeros y evitar el cruce que el curso pasado sí tuvo que disputar ante el Brujas.

articles.title: La meta es el Metropolitano
articles.standfirst: 36 equipos compiten por llegar a la gran final del 5 de junio; el PSG, bicampeón y favorito pese a su mal arranque en Francia
articles.summary: 36 equipos compiten por llegar a la gran final del 5 de junio; el PSG, bicampeón y favorito pese a su mal arranque en Francia
articles.body: La 72ª edición de la Copa de Europa, la 35ª bajo el formato Champions, ya está aquí. Arranca la Fase Liga para los 36 participantes con un fecha marcada en rojo en el calendario, en especial para el Atlético: la final del 5 de junio en el Metropolitano. El mejor escenario posible para que los de Diego Pablo Simeone 'entierren' las finales perdidas en Lisboa (2014) y en Milán (2016) y frente al Bayern en 1974. Habrá equipos de 16 Federaciones diferentes, pero LaLiga (Atlético, Barcelona, Betis, Real Madrid y Villarreal) y la Premier (Arsenal, Aston Villa, City, Liverpool y United) copan los 'bombos', con cinco participantes cada una. Les siguen la Bundesliga (Bayern, Borussia Dortmund, RB Leipzig y Stuttgart) y la Serie A (Como, Inter, Nápoles y Roma), con cuatro. El gran favorito, en cualquier caso, milita en la Ligue 1. El Paris Saint-Germain, campeón de las dos últimas ediciones, buscará igualar las tres Champions consecutivas que conquistó el Real Madrid de Zidane entre 2016 y 2018. "Los objetivos están claros: ganar títulos importantes... y no hay nada más importante que la Champions League", asegura Luis Enrique, que comenzará a defender su 'corona' mañana recibiendo al Slovan Bratislava de Yaya Touré. Sólo Carlo Ancelotti (5) acumula más 'orejonas' que 'Lucho', que ya la ganó con el Barcelona en 2015. Será, hablando de entrenadores, la primera Champions sin Pep Guardiola, campeón en 2009 y 2011 con el Barça y en 2023 con el City, desde la 2012-13. José Mourinho y 'Hansi' Flick ansían reescribir su nombre en el palmarés. 'The Special One', que hizo campeón a Oporto (2004) e Inter (2010) tras 17 y 45 años de sequía, confía en 'vengar' las tres eliminaciones consecutivas en semifinales que encadenó en su primera etapa en el banquillo del Real Madrid. Flick, ganador con el Bayern en 2020, quiere dar el paso que le falta tras guiar al Barcelona a levantar dos Ligas seguidas. Manuel Pellegrini tratará de conducir al Betis a las semifinales que ya alcanzó con el Villarreal (2005-06) y con el City (2015-16), mientras que para Iñigo Pérez, técnico del 'submarino amarillo' será su debut después de disputar la final de la Conference League con el Rayo. No lo tendrá fácil Luis Enrique... ni nadie. La Champions 2026-27 contará con 13 ganadores: Real Madrid (15), Bayern (6), Liverpool (6), Barcelona (5), Inter (3), Manchester United (3), PSG (2), Oporto (2), Borussia Dortmund (1), Manchester City (1), Feyenoord (1), Aston Villa (1) y PSV (1). De ahí que los partidazos en esta "semana exclusiva" en la que la UEFA ha reservado tres días para la Champions (martes, miércoles y jueves) estén garantizados: Real Madrid-Inter (hoy) y Liverpool-Atlético y Nápoles-Arsenal (mañana). Faltan, sin embargo, 24 Copas de Europa. Y es que hasta 11 campeones se han quedado fuera: Milan (7 títulos), Ajax (4), Juventus (2), Benfica (2), Chelsea (2), Nottingham Forest (2), Celtic (1), Hamburgo (1), Steaua (1), Olympique de Marsella (1) y Estrella Roja (1). No están tampoco, 18 de los 36 participantes, el 50%, de la pasada Champions. Se han caído Chelsea, Juventus, Bayer Leverkusen, Mónaco, Athletic, Newcastle, Eintracht... Contará, en cambio, con cuatro debutantes en la Fase Liga de la Champions: Como, LASK, Sabah y Viking. Para el Como de Cesc Fàbregas será su estreno en Europa, en cualquier torneo. Llama la atención, sobre todo, la presencia del Sabah. El campeón azerí, fundado en 2017, se medirá al Barcelona. El LASK Linz, que ya participó en la Copa de Europa 1965-66, regresa tras 61 años de ausencia. Por su parte, el Viking, que cuenta con un tándem formado por dos entrenadores, cayó ante el Barça de Cruyff en la 1ª ronda de la Champions 1992-93. Hay también regresos esperados, empezando por el Betis, que no participa en la Champions desde la 2005-06. Vuelve también el Fenerbahçe, ausente desde la 2008-09, y el Shakhtar Donetsk, que se verá obligado a jugar sus partidos en Stamford Bridge por la guerra de Ucrania. Que empiece ya.
