articles.title: Zan Vipotnik: The golden boot winner yet to kick start his season at Swansea City
articles.summary: Zan Vipotnik has been backed to return to form for Swansea City, even though he is still not guaranteed to return to the starting side.
articles.body:
Zan Vipotnik has been backed to return to form for Swansea City – even though he is still not guaranteed to return to the starting line-up.

Swansea are flying in the Championship, leading the table after six games, and they take their unbeaten start to Southampton on Tuesday (19:45 BST).

And yet their leading goalscorer of last season has not got up and running.

Vipotnik, 24, took the second-tier golden boot with 23 league goals last term for a side that did not trouble the eventual race for the play-offs.

The tally was built on an eye-catching start where he had bagged five goals from the opening six games.

The same number of appearances into the 2026-27 season, and Vipotnik is still to find the net.

The latest chance came in the latter stages of Saturday's goalless Welsh derby with Wrexham, Vipotnik having looked lively off the bench was unable to steer his stretch past Anthony Patterson to break the deadlock.

Swans boss Vitor Matos, though, appears calm.

Asked whether he expected the Slovenia international to find confidence and form soon, he replied: "I think if someone knows how to score goals it's him, so I think it's just a matter of scoring."

The obvious difference is that Vipotnik has only been given one league start so far this year, Adam Idah preferred in every game since the opening day win at Stoke City.

Idah, a £6m signing from Celtic a year ago, missed most of last season with injury, but has looked ready to make his mark with two goals so far.

Vipotnik stays at Swansea 'for the moment'

There have also been the question marks over Vipotnik's future.

There was the school of thought that Swansea might want to cash in on the high value of a player who out-performed his expected goals (xG) by some way last season.

In other words, he scored more goals than the chances suggested he had a right to.

The signing of Ross Stewart following the Scotland international's departure from Southampton only added weight to that theory.

But the only concrete bid was turned down, Hull City's £10m offer knocked back, while Matos claimed he was not aware of deadline day interest from Burnley.

The Portuguese did concede transfer windows still open elsewhere – most notably in Saudi Arabia – still mean a departure cannot be ruled out.

Former Wales striker Nathan Blake, who valued Vipotnik at around £25m, said the speculation and shift to the bench will have hit Vipotnik, claiming late last month: "I could see by looking at his face, he's not on it. He's probably two or three yards short mentally because of what is going on."

Last week Matos conceded it might have had an impact, saying: "It's normal that some things can unsettle you when we are in the middle of all of this."

'I'd want £30m for him' - Blake on Vipotnik

With Stewart injured for Tuesday's game with his former side, and Swansea likely to rotate for a third match in seven days, Matos was asked whether this was the game to reintroduce Vipotnik to the starting line-up.

"We need to see what is best for the team," said Matos, offering a smile but no commitment.

What he did offer, though, was conviction that the player of last season is still there in more ways than one.

"Besides the goals, he contributes a lot for the other parts of the game," said Matos.

"I think against Wrexham he came on really sharp with the right mindset, fought for the duels, fought for the first ball, second ball, tried to arrive in the box for that chance.

"Even with that he was helping building.

"So all that is coming - then it's just a matter of scoring and he will score for sure."

Swansea would welcome that as they look to show their impressive start should be taken seriously.

Their record of conceding just once so far is the meanest in the EFL, although they take on a Saints team who put five past Millwall last time out at St Mary's.

"Southampton I think is one of the best teams on the league, a proper contender to win the league and to get promoted," said Matos. "So it will be a really good game.

"We need to analyse the Wrexham game, see the priorities and then see as well Southampton.

"But I expect a really, really good game for us to compete."

articles.title: Joe Worrall: Centre-back aims to make Wrexham point after Burnley frustrations
articles.summary: Deadline day Wrexham signing Joe Worall says opportunities were "scarce" at Burnley, as he prepares to welcome his former side to the Racecourse.
articles.body:
Joe Worrall says he joined Wrexham to prove a Premier League point to himself - and former club Burnley.

The 29-year-old comes face-to-face again with former team-mates on Tuesday (19:45 BST), as Wrexham welcome a Clarets side yet to win this season and struggling at the bottom of the second tier after relegation last term.

Worrall left Burnley on deadline day having managed just eight league starts in two years at Turf Moor.

"It's always about the mentality and togetherness of a group, and Wrexham have it down to a tee."

In return, the Wrexham manager has hailed Worrall's early influence, adding that the defender has "been fantastic for us in terms of his personality", always a key focus point.

After two long away trips, Parkinson revealed his side had adapted their travelling and training schedule, culminating in a longer team meeting on Monday to stress their progress and the challenge of Burnley as the Red Dragons eye a first home win of the season.

It could see Wrexham line-up against Jamie Vardy, the former England and Leicester City striker who has signed for Burnley as a free agent after leaving Italian side Cremonese.

Vardy had been linked with Wrexham, who also landed an attacking option on deadline day in the form of Sheffield United's Callum O'Hare.

Parkinson said he would have a plan for whatever side Burnley put out while leaning on Worrall's knowledge of a dressing room he left a week ago.

"The division is very tight and very competitive," said the Wrexham boss.

"The games are divided by very tight margins. Burnley have got good players and we 100% respect their quality, but it's about concentrating on our own performance level."

articles.title: Mourinho, el Inter, Mbappé y Lautaro
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: La Champions trae al Bernabéu en el estreno del curso europeo a un rival de campanillas, el Inter, un equipo con el que Mourinho fue campeón de Europa precisamente en este escenario. Aquella victoria le proyectó al Madrid, que tenía mucho que agradecerle porque eliminando al Barça en la semifinal previa evitó al madridismo el sofoco de ver a los blaugrana jugar esa final en este escenario. En la sala de prensa, un colega italiano afincado en Madrid le regaló ayer un aspersor, recuerdo del intempestivo riego con el que el Camp Nou le obsequió como represalia por ello. De aquel primer paso de Mou por el Madrid quedó lo que quedó, que aun se discute cuánto fue. Esta segunda etapa la ha abierto con un talante muy distinto, cosa de agradecer. En lo deportivo todo está por escribirse de nuevo. Hasta ahora vemos un equipo bien reforzado en el verano, pero absolutamente fiado a que los artistas de la delantera resuelvan, sin que aparezca la dinámica de grupo que distingue a todo equipo bien armado. Hoy no será el día en que podamos verlo, porque este partido se afronta con una concentración de bajas en la media, tanto en jugadores de creación como creativos. No están disponibles ni Camavinga ni Bernardo Silva ni Güler, y Tchouaméni y Thiago Pitarch salen justo ahora de lesión, así que el único medio con el que de verdad se cuenta es Valverde, al que habrá que acompañar con dos a elegir entre Bellingham, retrasándole, Brahim, sacándole de la banda, el lateral Trent y el joven Cestero, al que Arbeloa cubrió de elogios pero apenas utilizó. Será, pues, una noche para salir del paso. Mourinho quitó importancia al partido, dado que este nuevo modelo de la Champions, que va por su tercer año, aplaza urgencias. Pero después de perder en La Cartuja una derrota europea bajo los focos del Bernabéu sentaría muy mal y aumentaría esa inquietud sobre si los delanteros colaboran lo suficiente en defensa, cuestión que empieza a molestar a Mbappé. El Inter viene con tres victorias en su liga pleno, y tras levantar un 0-2 al Nápoles en la última jornada, con dos de Lautaro, esa fiera del área. Peligro.

articles.title: No empecemos con esto, que no ha terminado
articles.standfirst: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.summary: 'Cuestiones mías', una opinión de Amalio Moratalla
articles.body: Ya estamos como siempre, pero antes que nunca. El Barcelona, estratosférico; el Madrid, que no va a poder; y el Atlético, que ha tirado la Liga en la jornada cuatro. Nada más lejos de la realidad. A día de hoy, las cosas están como vemos todos, pero hay que esperar las curvas. El Barcelona está muy bien, lidera, gana, supera con autoridad y golea sin nueve. Presiona hasta el infinito y algunos de los campeones del mundo ni siquiera son titulares. La conclusión precipitada de esta primera radiografía es que este equipo va a arrasar, pero no estamos ante un torneo corto. Hay que mantener muchos tableros vivos durante meses y, en contra de lo que parece, el Real Madrid —con su derrota incluida ante el Betis en Sevilla— está también muy bien. Afortunadamente le restan muchas jornadas a esta gran Liga. El Madrid, generando muchas ocasiones de gol, fallando un penalti —Mbappé— y jugando como le vi, me preocupa menos que al mirar la clasificación. Son dos equipos, Barça y Madrid, que van a sumar muchos puntos y, lejos de pensar que nuestra liga es una verbena, pienso lo contrario: igualdad, competitividad y diversión. Y meto en la quiniela también al Atlético, que, aun sumando cinco puntos menos de los posibles, lo veo un equipo poderoso, mejor que el de la pasada campaña, que tiene que acoplarse de atrás adelante y resolver lo de Julián, pero no va a ser lo que vimos en dos minutos de desajuste en San Mamés. Y si sigo con la clasificación, veo equipos armados, competitivos y que no se van a dejar arrebatar puntos con facilidad. Mi conclusión a día de hoy, también precipitada por los pocos minutos competidos, es que la Liga, nuestra liga, es una gran competición en la que hay buenos jugadores, buenos técnicos y magníficas aficiones que llenan los campos. Si nos dedicamos a destruirla en la jornada cuatro, mal vamos. No seremos ni justos ni sensatos. Aquí nadie ha tirado nada, nadie ha ganado nada y la clasificación general, la de los ‘Pichichis’ y ‘Zamoras’, la de las asistencias, etcétera, son solo fotos parciales de un primer tramo de competición que aún dará para mucho. Escucho a los cenizos hablar sobre nuestra competición liguera, pero me sugieren más una carcajada que una preocupación. Y si no está de acuerdo, eche un vistazo a lo que está pasando en Europa y entenderá lo que le digo.

articles.title: Deberían pasar los cinco de Champions
articles.standfirst: Una opinión de Roberto Gómez
articles.summary: Una opinión de Roberto Gómez
articles.body: Por segunda vez en su joven historia, el Metropolitano será la sede, el cinco de junio, de la final de la Champions. Sin duda, es el partido más importante del año y con un aliciente más, la inauguración de la Ciudad del Deporte. Que la final sea en el Metropolitano es un motivo de orgullo, pero también una presión añadida para los de Simeone que están másilusionados que nunca por conseguir la primera Orejona. El Atlético tiene un equipazo aunque es cierto que tiene el grupo más complicado. Pero es en el Metropolitano donde mejor se maneja y debería pasar. Lo mismo que el Villarreal de Iñigo Pérez, equipo de mucha calidad que necesita rodaje para afianzarse y, sobre todo, mejorar la imagen dada de la pasada edición con Marcelino. Debería pasar, al igual que el Betis. Los verdiblancos, además, han conseguido en La Cartuja ser un equipo difícil de ganar. Pellegrini tiene experiencia y una plantilla de calidad, con Isco y Ceballos que saben lo difícil que es ganar la Champions. Y faltan los dos claros favoritos: Real madrid y Barcelona. El Real Madrid siempre es favorito. Es su competición ideal. El madridismo vive para la Champions y con el plus de la final en Madrid y en el Metropolitano. Mourinho la ha ganado pero no con el Real Madrid y Mbappé está motivadísimo con la circunstancia que desde su marcha, el PSG ha ganado las dos últimas. El Barcelona de Flick, para muchos el mejor equipo del mundo, con Lamine, con Pedri, con Raphinha, un equipo que se pasea por España pero que en Champions le cuesta muchísimo. Es el grandísimo favorito y todo lo que no sea ganarla, sería otro fracaso histórico del equipo de Laporta. Veremos quien la gana, desde luego un español, pero lo más importante para medir el espectacular momento del fútbol español que la gane uno de los nuestros. Luis de la Fuente prepara ya la convocatoria para los próximos partidos de la selección española en Oviedo, Sevilla y Wembley frente a la histórica y potente selección de Inglaterra . El seleccionador no tiene intención de hacer muchos cambios. Es más, si puede repetirán todos los que ganaron el Mundial. Falta saber si Eric García podrá llegar. Las novedades podrían ser Camello, del Rayo, y Barrios, del Atlético. El Gobierno de España y la RFEF esperan la visita a nuestro país del presidente de la FIFA Gianni Infantino para hablar del próximo Mundial que se jugará en 2030. Infantino tiene claro que la final será en el Bernabéu como homenaje de al estadio blanco y al Real Madrid. Pero se tienen que decidir sedes y la organización del Mundial, cuya organización de momento se comparte con Portugal y Marruecos.

articles.title: La hora de Gulacsi en un escenario nada extraño para el portero del Villarreal
articles.standfirst: El guardameta apunta a debutar en una cancha que conoce de sobra tras jugar allí ocho partidos con el Leipzig
articles.summary: El guardameta apunta a debutar en una cancha que conoce de sobra tras jugar allí ocho partidos con el Leipzig
articles.body: La titularidad de Luiz Junior en la portería del Villarreal ha quedado más que en entredicho tras el calamitoso inicio de temporada firmado por el guardameta brasileño. Tras ser involuntario protagonista negativo en las primeras jornadas, su actuación el pasado fin de semana ante el Deportivo, puede haber sido la gota que ha colme el vaso de la paciencia y confianza que Iñigo Pérez había depositado en él durante los primeros partidos. La hora de Peter Gulacsi parece haber llegado y lo hará en un escenario que conoce a la perfección como es el Signal Iduna Park. El veterano portero húngaro, llegó este verano al equipo castellonense en lo que parecía una apuesta por la fiabilidad. La que ha mostrado durante más de una década como titular en las filas del Leipzig y la experiencia que denotan sus casi 50 partidos en una competición como la Liga de Campeones. A sus 36 años, y tras sus pasos por el Liverpool o Salzburgo antes de desembarcar en la Bundesliga, las ha visto de todos los colores, por lo que un partido como el de este martes en Alemania no es nada nuevo para él. Sin ir más lejos, la pasada temporada, y pocas semanas antes de que el Villarreal fuese vapuleado en Dortmund (4-0), Gulacsi arrancaba un punto con el Leipzig tras empatar a uno en el mismo escenario. Es el último de los ocho enfrentamientos que ha vivido allí hasta la fecha como guardameta titular, y justo en la mitad, su equipo regresó con un resultado positivo. Su balance allí es de 2 victorias, 2 empates y 4 derrotas. Su victoria más llamativa se remonta a la temporada 2021/22, cuando con el Leipzig golearon en Dortmund por 1-4, gracias entre otro al español Dabi Olmo, autor de uno de los goles. Por contra, su recuerdo más amargo se remonta a la temporada 2018/19, donde el marcador fue justamente a la inversa y fue goleado por un contundente 4-1.

articles.title: Piqué recuerda dos 'ilegalidades' del Madrid: "El gol de Mijatovic a la Juve y el de Sergio Ramos al Atlético"
articles.summary: Gerard Piqué le contestó a un usuario de TikTok que apuntó que "sólo hay una forma de que el F.C. Barcelona gane, y ya la conocemos".
articles.body: Gerard Piqué le contestó a un usuario de TikTok que apuntó que "sólo hay una forma de que el F.C. Barcelona gane, y ya la conocemos". El usuario le recordó al exfutbolista de 39 años su mano dentro del área en 2009 contra el Chelsea. Una jugada en la que el árbitro Tom Henning no pitó penalti, y en la que en su momento el defensa confesó en Sky Sports que tocó el balón con la mano "pero fue algo involuntario y creo que el árbitro tomó la decisión correcta". En ese partido el Chelsea reclamó hasta seis penaltis. "La conclusión es que nos han robado. Ha sido una injusticia", declaró el técnico Guus Hiddink tras el 1-1 entre Chelsea y Barcelona en el día del célebre 'Iniestazo' en Stamford Bridge. "Bueno @mrvdm... Sí, sólo hay una forma de que gane el Barça, y es jugando muy bien al fútbol. Por eso somo reconocidos. Hemos ganado muchas Ligas, muchas Champions y muchos tripletes jugando muy bien al fútbol", empezó argumentando Piqué. Posteriormente el exjugador del Barcelona le recordó algunos errores arbitrales a favor del Madrid en Champions: "Siempre habéis sacado vosotros el tema de los árbitros. Te recuerdo la final de la Champions contra la Juventus, el gol de Mijatovic, que es ilegal. O dos de las finales del Atlético de Madrid contra el Real Madrid, el gol de Sergio Ramos es en fuera de juego también. Es ilegal". "Así que, errores arbitrales hay muchos normalmente. Históricamente, siempre han ido un poquito más a favor del Real Madrid. Así que nada, por lo demás, espero que estés bien, un fuerte abrazo y a disfrutar el día", subrayó.

articles.title: Aston Villa: No goals as Unai Emery rebuilds Villa's forward line in a new era
articles.summary: Aston Villa have not scored in their opening three Premier League games - how will manager Unai Emery find their attacking edge?
articles.body:
It is a new era - but Aston Villa have been here before.

No goals in their first three Premier League games, with one shot on target, has followed a summer of change.

They open their second Champions League campaign under Unai Emery at Club Brugge on Tuesday aiming to ignite the season.

Villa took five games to score their first top-flight goal last season before ending the campaign triumphant, winning the Europa League in Istanbul.

Since then, six of the starting XI from that victory have departed Villa Park, leaving them rebuilding their forward line.

Record £65m buy Nicolas Jackson has replaced Ollie Watkins, while Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alejandro Garnacho have arrived following Morgan Rogers' £117m move to Chelsea .

Emery has revamped Villa before, but can he find their new attacking edge?

Watch highlights of every Champions League game from 22:00 on Wednesday on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app. There will also be a Champions League Match of the Day on BBC One on Wednesday, from 22:40 to 00:00. This week there will also be be a highlights show on Thursday on BBC Two at 22:30 with highlights from Thursday's matches dropping at 22:00.

Watkins' departure to Al-Hilal - which lurched between acrimonious and emotional - has left Villa without their best attacking outlet.

Despite just one goal in his first 13 top-flight games last season he ended with 16 to leave for £51m on 91 Premier League goals, a club record.

Jackson was brought in as Watkins' direct replacement and was a priority signing for Emery having worked with him at Villarreal.

Emery gave the Senegal striker his debut at Estadio de la Ceramica and believes he can rely on him to fill the void Watkins has left.

He has started Villa's past two games, the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal and Saturday's draw at Hull.

Jackson scored 30 goals in 81 appearances for Chelsea and the stats slightly favour England's Watkins, when they both played in the Premier League between 2023 and 2025.

In his first Premier League season the 25-year-old scored 14 goals and assisted five, compared with Watkins' 19 goals and 13 assists.

In 2024-25 Jackson scored 10 goals to Watkins' 16 in 382 fewer minutes. He only had eight fewer shots but his conversion rate of 13.2% was inferior to Watkins' of 19.1%.

Jackson's touches in the box are also lower than Villa's departed striker - 168-231 in 2023-24 and 153-182 in 2024-25.

Yet, Jackson's time at Bayern Munich - helping them win the Bundesliga last season - gave him a 21.1% conversion rate, scoring eight goals in 1,004 minutes of game time.

It is why Emery trusts Jackson, but the unknown is being able to gel a new core of players together, however high their potential.

Emery also has to ensure Mbaye - a £47m arrival from Paris St-Germain on deadline day - and Garnacho can provide Jackson the ammunition.

Between them, Watkins and Rogers scored 46% of Villa's goals in the Premier League last season.

Rogers and Lucas Digne provided 12 assists, with Youri Tielemans adding four and Watkins three.

All four have left, so 18-year-old Mbaye and Chelsea loanee Garnacho will be expected to be the supply line, with Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham supporting Jackson.

Garnacho has, so far, been kept out by George Hemmings - the 19-year-old is highly rated at Villa Park with Emery calling him "clearly a Premier League player".

But the academy product only had 25 minutes of top-flight football before this season so expectations must be managed.

Argentina winger Garnacho created six big chances, earning four assists, at Chelsea last term but scored just once.

Mbaye created four goals in 10 starts for PSG last season, helping them win Ligue 1, and was an unused substitute at Hull on Saturday. Emery will expect more from both once they are in tune with his demands.

Manzambi, one of the World Cup's breakout stars in the summer, has yet to play for Villa after his move from Freiburg as he recovers from a knee injury.

Emery's messaging is crucial, which is why it will take time for them to develop into the cohesive unit the manager demands.

His meetings can last anywhere between 90 minutes and two hours, which naturally tests players' focus levels, but underlines the amount of detail they need to take on board.

To integrate 10 new players, including Jackson, Mbaye and Garnacho, takes time. It is time Emery usually likes to use carefully - but it something he does not have in the current circumstances.

It is why, when he needed players in January, Douglas Luiz returned on loan from Juventus and Abraham arrived from Besiktas.

Luiz knew Emery's methods and Abraham at least knew the club, although neither deal worked - with Luiz returning to Italy and Emery willing to let Abraham go this summer only for the striker to decide to stay.

Only two summer signings - Jackson and goalkeeper Zion Suzuki - started the draw at Hull and Taylor Harwood-Bellis was left out of the squad, underlining the situation Emery must deal with.

"We must be patient, and we should understand that we are rebuilding the team. Now they must get our way and demands, keeping the same mentality that we built, but with different players," said Emery.

"Now is no time to think two weeks or three weeks forward.

"We must try to focus on each match. The next match is the Champions League and something we can feel excited and motivated to play because we deserve to be there.

"Now it is to compete in Brugge on Tuesday. Then, we are going to think about the next match at home against Nottingham Forest .

"Each match is a lot of information we can have. We are collecting information individually and collectively about the players, about the structure, about the capacity to build the team.

"Saturday was one point. It was not enough, but I am feeling optimistic about how the players are responding."

articles.title: Scariolo avala a Mourinho para reconstruir al Madrid: “Es la persona adecuada”
articles.standfirst: El técnico italiano analizó en 'La Tribu' el Real Madrid-Inter de Champions y defendió que el portugués tiene “experiencia, carisma y autoridad” para ordenar el talento blanco
articles.summary: El técnico italiano analizó en 'La Tribu' el Real Madrid-Inter de Champions y defendió que el portugués tiene “experiencia, carisma y autoridad” para ordenar el talento blanco
articles.body: Sergio Scariolo pasó por La Tribu en la previa de uno de los grandes partidos de la primera jornada de la Champions: el Real Madrid-Inter. Un cruce especial para el técnico italiano, interista confeso y simpatizante del conjunto blanco, que analizó el momento de ambos equipos y dejó una reflexión muy clara sobre José Mourinho. Preguntado por los problemas defensivos del Madrid y por la exigencia que rodea a futbolistas como Mbappé, Vinicius o Bellingham, Scariolo señaló directamente al banquillo. “Para eso está Mourinho”, afirmó. Para el entrenador, el portugués es “la persona adecuada” para completar el talento de los jugadores con “ética, esfuerzo, compañerismo y sentido del equipo”. Scariolo defendió que Mourinho reúne las condiciones necesarias para intentar corregir los vicios del equipo blanco. “Si hay un entrenador con la experiencia, el carisma, la autoridad para poder hacer esos cambios”, explicó, aunque recordó que ese tipo de transformaciones “no se producen de la noche a la mañana” y requieren tiempo. El técnico italiano también matizó que no todo depende del entrenador, aunque se llame Mourinho. Para que el Madrid pueda crecer, insistió en que la visión debe estar compartida por los jugadores y por el club: “Si todo el mundo está en la misma página, evidentemente se podrá ir creciendo”. Desde su experiencia como seleccionador y gestor de grandes vestuarios, Scariolo comparó el desafío de Mourinho con la dificultad de repartir papeles en equipos llenos de talento. El italiano recordó que, al máximo nivel, muchas veces la clave no está solo en la pizarra, sino en convencer a los jugadores de remar en la misma dirección, incluso cuando el rol no es el que desean. “Este es un deporte de equipo”, subrayó. Scariolo explicó que los roles deben quedar claros desde el principio, aunque luego puedan cambiar con explicaciones lógicas. Para él, ningún técnico puede sostener su autoridad únicamente en el “porque yo lo digo”; debe motivar sus decisiones y hacer entender que responden al bien del equipo. Sobre el camino del Real Madrid, Scariolo pidió paciencia. Considera que el equipo necesita coherencia, cohesión y que todos, “desde el vértice del club hasta todo el cuerpo técnico”, remen en la misma dirección. Si eso ocurre, defendió, “antes o después las cosas llegan”. Esa idea sirvió también para comparar al Madrid con el Inter. Scariolo destacó que el conjunto italiano mantiene una personalidad reconocible pese a los cambios de entrenador y de plantilla. El 3-5-2 sigue siendo el guion principal y futbolistas como Calhanoglu, Lautaro, Barella, Dimarco o Bastoni sostienen una continuidad competitiva que explica su estabilidad. El técnico italiano también puso contexto al momento del Inter. Recordó que el club ha mantenido una gran regularidad a nivel nacional, pero que el último paso en Europa está condicionado por la dificultad para acceder a grandes estrellas. “El Inter no puede fichar a un top player”, señaló, antes de recordar que no puede gastar 80 millones en un futbolista y que incluso ha tenido que vender para mantener su competitividad. Scariolo puso en valor la capacidad del club italiano para reciclar jugadores, detectar oportunidades de mercado y sostener un bloque reconocible pese a no manejar los presupuestos de otros gigantes europeos. Aun así, admitió que la gran expectativa vuelve a estar en comprobar si el Inter puede repetir gestas como las finales de Champions alcanzadas en los últimos años. La entrevista también sirvió para conocer el momento personal de Scariolo tras un verano diferente. El técnico explicó que sigue muy cerca del juego a través de su colaboración con el BC Roma, proyecto liderado por Luka Doncic, viendo entrenamientos a diario y ayudando a los entrenadores con una visión “exclusivamente técnica”. Aun así, dejó abierta la puerta a volver pronto a entrenar. “Yo soy entrenador”, afirmó, antes de explicar que quizá dentro de un mes esté de nuevo en primera línea o que puede continuar este año vinculado al juego desde otra posición. El duelo por su salida, aseguró, ya está pasado: “Eres profesional y lo asimilas rápido”. Scariolo, interista por herencia familiar y con Sandro Mazzola como primer gran ídolo, vivirá el Real Madrid-Inter con el corazón dividido. Pero su análisis dejó una idea central en clave blanca: si el Madrid necesita ordenar talento, roles y exigencia colectiva, Mourinho es, para él, el técnico indicado para intentarlo.

articles.title: Francesco Farioli: Porto boss out to stun Man City in Champions League
articles.summary: Porto boss Francesco Farioli is one of the most highly regarded young managers and on Tuesday he takes charge in the Champions League for the first time.
articles.body:
Francesco Farioli is one of the fastest-rising stars in coaching.

The 37-year-old led Porto to the Portuguese title last season and is now preparing to take charge of his first Champions League match as a manager against Manchester City at the Estadio do Dragao on Tuesday.

Leading a team out in Europe's premier club competition might still feel a long time coming for Farioli, who was linked with the vacancies at Chelsea, Liverpool and Rangers last season.

However, Farioli, who began his managerial journey in Turkey in 2021 with Fatih Karagumruk and then Alanyaspor, opted to renew his contract instead and is certain he made the right choice.

"I don't feel I could be in a better place," he told BBC Sport.

"I said at our post-season dinner they have created a problem for me, as I will have to bring the president and directors with me."

Chief among the relationships keeping him at Porto has been the one with club president Andre Villas-Boas, the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager.

Watch highlights of every Champions League game from 22:00 on Wednesday on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app. There will also be a Champions League Match of the Day on BBC One on Wednesday, from 22:40 to 00:00. This week there will also be be a highlights show on Thursday on BBC Two at 22:30 with highlights from Thursday's matches dropping at 22:00.

Another key figure in his story is current Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi, who appointed Farioli - then a former non-league goalkeeper in Italy and blogger on the Wyscout coaching platform - on to his backroom staff at Benevento in 2017 and then took him to Sassuolo.

Initially a goalkeeping coach, he moved into management in Turkey before successful spells at Nice in France and Dutch club Ajax.

His time at Ajax did, though, end in disappointment, with the club missing out on the Eredivisie title on the final day. That came after a turbulent January transfer window, during which he felt they had failed to strengthen sufficiently.

The season before his arrival, Ajax had briefly been involved in a relegation battle.

"I am used to entering uncomfortable situations where there is a lack of direction and things are not in place," Farioli said.

"I was looking for a club with a similar spirit, not for revenge, but one that wanted to put things right."

He said Porto had felt the "same pain" after finishing third before his arrival and shared "the same ambition to do something special".

On meeting Villas-Boas in the Italian city of Como before accepting the job, Farioli was reassured to find the club's vision aligned with his own.

Porto won the Portuguese Super Cup last month and will have designs on causing an upset against Enzo Maresca's City. As former European champions who lifted the trophy under Jose Mourinho in 2004, they possess considerable Champions League pedigree.

How Farioli has developed a distinct identity

It is not just Farioli's rise through the game that has attracted attention. Across spells at Nice, Ajax and now Porto, his teams have developed a distinctive identity built on possession, structure and aggressive pressing.

Porto have started this season with five wins out of five, conceding only one goal in the league.

This is the result of impressive tactical understanding alongside a focus on the human part of coaching individuals.

A fitting example of Farioli tying these two parts of management together was seen in the form of an anonymous questionnaire he gave his players about his tactics, allowing the squad to make suggestions.

Farioli produced teams with the best domestic defensive records while in charge of Nice, Ajax and Porto but this does not come from being a 'defensive coach'.

"One year earlier in Ajax, I was accused of being too offensive," he said. "Now in Porto, I was accused of being too defensive. It's probably not one way or another but it is just about balancing the team."

When asked what contributed to his sides being so strong defensively, he referred to this balance between attack and defence.

"A part that is quite underestimated is the part on the ball," he explained. "You cannot really separate moments. These are phases of the same cycle.

"This defensive record comes a lot also from the way that we attack, the type of structure that we want when attacking and how we prepare ourselves in the moment that we lose the ball. Everything is linked."

Porto look to hold the ball for long periods of the game, remaining stationed closer to the opposition goal.

As they attack, they maintain a solid structure of players behind the ball ready to defend counter-attacks.

Around the Porto player on the ball, team-mates are positioned close enough to apply pressure as soon as the ball is lost too - hoping to regain possession quickly.

And this aggressive pressure is not only seen when Porto lose the ball, also coming into play when opponents look to build out from the back.

Porto press high, at times asking three attackers to stifle the build-up of a back five or six, but they manage to prevent opponents finding their free player, a seemingly impossible task.

"A lot goes with understanding and timing, specific triggers, and the capacity for the players to interpret the moment of the game according to where we are on the pitch and what the opponent is trying to do," he added.

"We spend a lot of work on video, correction and explanation. You need players capable to understand and to put the extra effort. The collaboration between players is key."

Returning to Farioli's intertwined approach of using attacking moments to defend and defensive moments to attack, Porto's press does not just look to force opponent's long.

Instead, they entice them to play into the centre of the pitch before looking to win it back, setting them up nicely to attack the goal against a disorganised defence.

"The way that we approach these moments is something I started in my first experience in Turkey, to apply ideas and implement a method. But again, it's not just about the moment off the ball, it's also about the way to attack.

"Something that we experienced a lot with Roberto de Zerbi was to play with certain distances, to have a team very narrow on the ball. It's a way to facilitate the transition moment and to rebalance when we lose the ball, to avoid counter-attacks.

"I believe that football, and life in general, is made by two principles: entropy, meaning chaos, and negative entropy, the intention to bring order.

"As a coach, I can help the team by bringing more order, a language and maybe some glasses to see the reality and how to see the game in the same way."

With Porto facing City on Tuesday, he has the chance to test his ideas against one of the world's best teams.

articles.title: Como extend forward Roberta Picchi's contract after cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Italian club Como renew the contract of forward Roberta Picchi after she is diagnosed with breast cancer.
articles.body:
Como have extended the contract of their forward Roberta Picchi after she was diagnosed with breast cancer.

The Italian club, who will make their women's Serie A debut this season, said they extended Picchi's contract until the end of the 2027-28 season as part of their "continued commitment" to the player.

The 34-year-old Italian is set to begin cancer treatment and will be supported by Como's medical team, who will work with the ​specialists overseeing her care.

"Everyone at Como ​1907 is alongside Roberta and will give her and her family all the ​support they need during the ​months ahead," the club said in a statement.

"At this time, we ask that Roberta's privacy is respected as she focuses on her treatment ​and recovery."

Picchi was part of the Como side that finished 11 points clear of Lumezzane as they claimed the Serie B title last season to earn their first promotion to the top division of Italian women's football.

"Nothing ​should ever be taken for ​granted, ⁠and I feel fortunate," Picchi wrote on social media.

"It's time to play my match, but ⁠I'll ​be back even ​more determined."

Como, managed by Selena Mazzantini, begin their season against AC Milan on 26 September.

articles.title: Real’s Mbappe embraces Ballon d’Or talk after historic World Cup goals
articles.summary: Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe enters Champions League season hoping for Ballon d’Or after record World Cup goal haul.
articles.body:
Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe says it is natural for people to consider him a potential Ballon d’Or winner this year after his World Cup exploits.

The France captain scored 10 goals at the tournament this summer to win the Golden Boot, with his country finishing fourth. He has netted 22 in the competition, making him the World Cup’s all-time top scorer.

Mbappe, 27, has not yet won the prestigious trophy given to the world’s best player.

“I think that when you play for Real Madrid, which is the best club in the world, naturally people associate you with that kind of award, they associate you with collective awards, individual awards,” Mbappe told reporters.

“A lot of people, when they see me in the street, talk to me about the Ballon d’Or, a lot of people talk about me as a possible Ballon d’Or winner … Of course, I made a lot of history this summer in the most important competition in sport, but we’ll see.

“I have the feeling that it’s a good year for that, but there’s still a long time to go, and people are free to vote for whoever they think is the best player in the world.”

Since joining Real Madrid in 2024, Mbappe has scored huge quantities of goals, but the club has failed to win a major trophy.

On Tuesday, the record 15-time European champions host Inter Milan in the Champions League in the first match of the league phase.

During Mbappe’s first two years at Madrid, the team has appeared unbalanced, with many star names, including the Frenchman and Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, widely considered not to be contributing enough to the team effort – in contrast to Ousmane Dembele at Paris Saint-Germain and Raphinha at Barcelona.

“We have to improve,” admitted Mbappe. “But I could play dumb and tell you that I score more goals than [Dembele and Raphinha], and that they need to score more goals to be like me.

“Everyone is different, but I want to do things intelligently and say that of course I have to improve and all that, but I don’t like comparisons because I think I do a lot of things that others don’t do.”

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho recently said he would prefer if Mbappe scored fewer goals but also worked hard to help the team win titles.

Mbappe said he would accept lower numbers if it led to trophies, but noted they were not mutually exclusive.

“I’d take 30 goals with titles, yes, but… for me it’s an absurd debate,” said Mbappe.

“I always want to score goals and win titles … you don’t have to choose, you can do both things.”

Veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho led Inter to Champions League glory in 2010 at the Santiago Bernabeu before he departed to take over at Real Madrid.

Despite his history with the Italian side, whom he steered to the treble that year, the coach said that only mattered before and after, but not during the match.

“There aren’t many [people] left from my time, but it’ll always be a pleasure to see people, even if I don’t know them, but people who defend Inter, before and after,” said Mourinho.

“During the game I want to win, they want to win, and there won’t be time to think about things from a wonderful past.”

Inter coach Cristian Chivu started the 2010 final playing under his opposite number on Tuesday at the Bernabeu.

“Mourinho is a special person, and I was lucky to have encountered him,” said Chivu, who described the Portuguese as a “winner”.

“There are few in the world like him,” continued the Romanian coach.

“He showed it here but at other big clubs too. I’m sure Real Madrid will have a great season.”

Mourinho wants his Madrid players to bounce back from their first defeat of the season, 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday in La Liga.

“I want to win. I could tell you I want to play well, but I don’t want to play well like we did against Betis and lose,” added Mourinho.

articles.title: Gioacchini abre el 'bote de ketchup' y hace soñar al Sabadell
articles.standfirst: El delantero estadounidense suma cuatro goles en tres partidos
articles.summary: El delantero estadounidense suma cuatro goles en tres partidos
articles.body: "Marcar goles es como abrir un bote de ketchup: lo más difícil es abrir el bote. Cuando está abierta ya está". Lo dijo Nicholas Gioacchini en su puesta de largo como nuevo delantero del Sabadell después de una pretemporada sin puntería y se ha cumplido. El delantero estadounidense se ha erigido en el hombre gol de la gran sorpresa de este inicio de temporada en LaLiga Hypermotion. Marcó el gol de la victoria en el reencuentro de la Nova Creu Alta con la categoría cinco años después, contra el Almería (1-0), y este lunes abrió el camino hacia el triunfo contra el Córdoba con un doblete fulgurante (3-2), en once minutos. También vio portería en la victoria contra el Barça Atlètic en la final de la Copa Catalunya: son cuatro goles en los últimos tres encuentros. El '16' arlequinado ya es segundo en la clasificación de máximos artilleros de la categoría de plata, solo por detrás del gironí Yáser Asprilla. Gioacchini, de 26 años, es un delantero desconocido para el fútbol español que recaló en la Nova Creu Alta a prueba hace unas semanas y convenció a Ferran Costa. Salió desde el banquillo en la primera jornada y ya ha sido titular en las tres siguientes. A este ritmo será difícil sacarle del once. Gioacchini pretende relanzar su carrera en Sabadell, recuperar el nivel que le llevó a la selección absoluta de Estados Unidos con apenas 20 años. En 2021 fue campeón de la Copa de Oro, con una participación destacada: dio la asistencia del gol para llegar a la final y participó en cinco de los seis encuentros, incluido el duelo por el título contra México. Desde entonces había protagonizado altibajos y acabó en Grecia, sin hueco en el Como de Cesc Fábregas. Ahora ha llegado al fútbol español, del que se ha declarado un enamorado. "Disfruto el fútbol español. Es un fútbol técnico, creativo: no solo chutar, correr y esperar. Es mi fútbol favorito y estoy muy orgulloso de poder vivir esta oportunidad y de poder apreciar lo que aporta este país al fútbol", dijo en su presentación. También hizo suya la frase que dijo en su día Ruud van Nistelrooy: "Los goles son como el ketchup. A veces, por más que aprietes, no sale nada. Y luego sale todo de golpe". El Sabadell es tercero e invicto y Gioacchini vuelve a sonreír.

articles.summary: Los detalles del duelo de la máxima competición europea
articles.body: El AEK de Atenas inicia su andadura en la fase de grupos de la UEFA Champions League recibiendo al LASK austríaco en el OPAP Arena. El conjunto heleno, dirigido por el serbio Marko Nikolic, pretende hacer valer la veteranía y el jerarquía de su plantilla para sumar los primeros tres puntos en Europa. Tras incorporar este verano a futbolistas de primer nivel contrastado como el goleador serbio Luka Jovic —que aterriza tras firmar 21 dianas la pasada campaña— o el centrocampista croata Lovro Majer, los atenienses confían en su fortaleza como locales para arrancar la competición con buen pie. Por su parte, el LASK se presenta en la capital griega ostentando la etiqueta de una de las grandes revelaciones del torneo tras culminar una histórica y heroica remontada frente al Celtic en el 'playoff'. El cuadro de Linz, que certificó su regreso a la máxima competición continental tras décadas de ausencia, se encomienda a la pegada en ataque de Kalajdzic y a la velocidad vertiginosa de extremos como Usor y Adeniran. Sin nada que perder y con la moral por las nubes, la escuadra austríaca buscará dar un nuevo golpe sobre la mesa y mantener viva su ilusionante travesía europea. El partido entre el AEK Atenas y el LASK, correspondiente a la jornada 1 de la UEFA Champions League, se disputará este martes 8 de septiembre a las 18:45 horas (horario peninsular español) en el OPAP Arena de Atenas. El encuentro entre el AEK Atenas y el LASK se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España a través de la plataforma Movistar+, en el canal M+ Liga de Campeones 2 o M+ Liga de Campeones 3. articles.title: Joao Moutinho at 40: Braga midfielder's incredible longevity explained as he passes 1,150 professional appearances
articles.summary: As Joao Moutinho turns 40, Adam Bate looks at how the Portuguese midfielder manages to keep going as he embarks on his 23rd consecutive top-flight season in Europe; featuring insight from Carlos Carvalhal, his coach at Sporting and Braga, as well as the man himself
articles.body:
He played the full 90 minutes in the away leg of the tie against Dinamo Minsk in Bulgaria. He lasted the distance away to Austria Vienna too, before also playing the whole match as Braga won the Derby do Minho against Vitor Guimaraes just days later.

Moutinho turns 40 years old on the eighth day of September and he is already nine games into yet another season having played his final game as a thirtysomething away to Alverca on Saturday. Braga won. Moutinho played the entire game. Of course he did.

He passed the 1,000 game mark as long ago as 2024 and has now made at least 25 appearances for his club in 23 consecutive seasons. There were 56 games for him last season, the seventh time he has passed the half-century mark in a campaign.

Moutinho is a supremely gifted footballer, a European champion with Portugal and a title winner in France as well as his home country. He went on to become arguably Wolves' greatest-ever Premier League player during his five seasons in England.

But his longevity is becoming his most remarkable trait. Braga are already the fifth club he has brought up a century of games for, and could yet become the fourth different club he has represented at least 200 times. How is he able to keep going?

There was a clue when visiting the training ground to interview him back in his Wolves days. Every other player had left. Moutinho was having an ice bath and a massage. "I like playing more than training so I try to be fit to play," he explained that afternoon.

"I do what I need to do to stay fit. Train well. I eat well. I drink water and hydration drinks. I rest when I need to rest. I come to training every day as if it is the first day. They are small things but they make a difference." For Moutinho, this was as natural as breathing.

"I work a lot in the gym on injury prevention. This is important too. You have to believe in this work. You cannot just do it because you do it. You have to recognise that if you do this it is good for your body and it will give you something extra that will then help you."

Carlos Carvalhal is perhaps better placed than anyone to explain Moutinho's endurance. He coached him at Sporting when he was an emerging player and again at Braga 14 years later. "I do not remember any kind of injury," Carvalhal tells Sky Sports .

"He is a guy who knows his body exactly, he knows the limits." When it comes to his footballing brain, however, those limits are not so obvious. Carvalhal talks of an in-built GPS and how even when he was a youngster Moutinho was his conductor on the pitch.

"He played in a different position. At that time, he was an offensive midfielder. At Braga, we put him as a number six. We thought that was the best position for him now because he is not young any more. But he still understands everything about the game."

The touch remains immaculate, the decision-making spot on. Physically, the Portuguese league is perhaps a better environment for him now than the cut and thrust of the Premier League but he is able to use his vast experience to get through games.

"He anticipates everything. He balances everything." For Carvalhal, he was key. "He was unbelievable, fantastic." And as a Braga man, the coach has been following him even since he himself left. "Last season it was the same, another fantastic season again."

The minutes are being managed more than they used to be. Moutinho is becoming something of a Thursday night specialist for Braga. Not that he likes it. "He is still frustrated if the coach pulls him out after 75 minutes. He wants to play all the games."

That chimes with what team-mates have always said. Ruben Neves once called him the most competitive man he had met. Putting that comment to Moutinho at Wolves' training ground, he replied: "Years ago, it was worse. I wouldn't talk to my family [after a defeat]."

Moutinho explained: "I don't like to lose, no matter what I am playing. Football, tennis, head tennis, no matter what. If I am playing, I am playing to win. If I am not playing to win, I don't want to play. There needs to be something that moves you, that inspires you.

"I think it is good for the spirit to have that mentality. You cannot be different when it comes to the small things. Play to win something every day. If you live like that every day then, of course, at the weekend you are going to be winning." That mentality remains.

But for how long? Moutinho's latest contract is up at the end of the season but that was the case last year and the year before that. "We do not know when he will stop," says Carvalhal, smiling. "Because if he stays playing at this level, it is not a question of age."

He adds: "It is a question of performance and how you deal with this. He deals with it fantastically. Some play at 40 but not at the level of Moutinho. He is playing at the full level all the time. If he does another season like last season, I believe he will play on."

Braga's next game is against Estrela on Thursday. Their European campaign resumes in Copenhagen next month, days after facing one of Moutinho's old clubs Sporting. History would suggest he will be fit and ready to go. "It is unbelievable, something unique."

articles.title: Riccardo Calafiori: How Arsenal's defender has emerged as one of the Premier League's best left-backs
articles.summary: Riccardo Calafiori has been called "the best left-back in the Premier League by far" by Jamie Carragher; the Italian has started the season with a goal in the Community Shield and two assists against Coventry and Aston Villa; Sky Sports' Sam Blitz analyses Calafiori's wild positioning
articles.body:
When Arsenal came in for Calafiori, he was regularly playing at centre-back at Bologna. Those who guided his career had doubts about whether he could reach the highest level as a left-back.

But now, Calafiori is not just thriving as a left-back for the Premier League champions. "He's the best left-back in the league by far," says Jamie Carragher.

As well as being part of an imperious Arsenal defence, the Italian has started this season on fire in front of goal, scoring in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and getting assists in the league victories over Coventry and Aston Villa.

VAR spotting an offside Ezri Konsa denied Calafiori getting on the scoresheet against Chelsea, but the Italian did have a crucial role in Arsenal's winning goal, scored by Martin Odegaard.

In the build-up, Calafiori's run inside of Christos Tzolis helped drag Pedro Neto into a back five - putting more Chelsea players behind the ball and rubberstamping Arsenal's dominance on the game.

"He dictated the formation of Chelsea," said Carragher, analysing the goal on Sky Sports. "Wherever Calafiori was, Neto was. When Calafiori drops forward, Neto drops into make a back five.

"Chelsea were flittering between a back four in the main and a back five. It's all about the positioning of Calafiori."

But that was not all. Calafiori kept going.

His run into the penalty area then dragged centre-back Maxence Lacroix with him and created a 14.4-yard gap between the Chelsea defender and his partner Wesley Fofana.

That was all the space Arsenal needed for Kai Havertz to dummy the ball to Odegaard, who finished with ease.

But again, that's not all. Because we've seen that exact same move from Arsenal before.

Arsenal's third goal in the Community Shield win over City had the same characteristics. A run and ball in from Tzolis, a dummy from Havertz - and Odegaard comfortably scoring.

But crucially, it had the same underlapping run made by Calafiori - which created the same large centre-back gap between Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol.

"You see the space between the centre-backs, that comes from Calafiori," added Carragher. "This is the impact he's having on games at left-back."

But can his position really be described as 'left-back', given Calafiori is effectively operating as an extra attacker for this Arsenal team? The Italian has a habit of popping up everywhere, from centre forward to right wing.

It was seen in the first half against Chelsea, when Calafiori ventured from the left to the right flank in the same attacking move - taking just eight seconds to pop up in a completely different role.

"That's Ricci though!" said former Arsenal winger Leandro Trossard in November when asked by Sky Sports about Calafiori's wild positioning.

"He pops up everywhere - in the pockets, as a striker - that unpredictability can hurt teams.

"I know what he can do and where he can pop up in what position. Sometimes I can play a ball blind to him and I know he will be there."

It seems, on the basis of the goals Odegaard scored against Man City and Chelsea, that Calafiori has a similar understanding building with new winger Tzolis.

It is not just Calafiori who does this, as Ben White is also tasked with taking rogue positions in the Arsenal attack. He was also seen in a hybrid centre-forward role during the Chelsea game at times.

While White tends to take the role of a more traditional full-back compared to Calafiori's maverick positioning, his tactical flexibility is summed up by the fact that he ranks top of overlapping runs in the Premier League this season, and fourth for underlapping runs.

"Playing full-back the way he [Mikel Arteta] wants is, I think, completely different to any other manager," White told Sky Sports in the 2023-24 season.

"To play full-back for him, you've got to be a centre mid, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10."

When fully fit, Arsenal are a well-oiled machine that are a nightmare to prepare for tactically. "They push you to the limits," said Xabi Alonso after his Chelsea team came away from the Emirates with a 2-1 defeat.

Every player has to be accounted for in defending. No player can be left unmarked or unwatched for long. Calafiori is the epitome of why Arsenal are so difficult to play against.

It shows why so many teams revert to a low block against Arsenal. There are so many attackers to play against. And if you try to take Arsenal on - thereby opening yourselves up in defence - you get what Chelsea got.

articles.title: Ross Wilson: Newcastle chief reveals club prepared for Eddie Howe exit in summer that 'never felt chaotic'
articles.summary: Newcastle chief Ross Wilson reveals club were prepared for Eddie Howe's exit; Magpies also lost key players this summer, including captain Bruno Guimaraes; Wilson admits midfielder's Arsenal exit was not "part of plan" - but Wilson insists: "[This summer] never felt chaotic inside"
articles.body:
Howe's shock resignation in July led to the swift appointment of Matthias Jaissle , who has enjoyed an unbeaten start to his reign.

Howe's exit was part of a turbulent summer for the Magpies which also included the departures of key players Bruno Guimaraes , Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon .

Toon chief Wilson revealed Howe's resignation was not "painful" because of their Jaissle contingency, but Guimaraes' £75m move to Arsenal was not "part of the plan".

Wilson said: "Eddie is an exceptionally talented coach and at some point that meant he was probably going to do something else and we had to be prepared for that.

"It didn't feel painful. Clearly the timing was not one we had planned for. But we had a plan in place which is why we executed it as quickly as we did.

"It might have caught some people off guard, but the reason we could move so quickly on it was because we had prepared for a number of months."

Wilson added: "I think we want Newcastle United to be a club with anticipation and excitement. If we're not it probably means we're doing it wrong.

"[This summer] never felt chaotic inside. There is no point us pretending otherwise - we did not want to lose Bruno Guimaraes. That was really disappointing that we got to that place in the end.

"We were happy where we got to in terms of numbers but that was not part of our plan. But everything else that happened during the window was part of the plan."

'Trading an important part of Newcastle plan'

Wilson believes success for Newcastle rests on them being a trading club going forwards after a summer of fluctuating fortunes in the transfer window.

Newcastle raised nearly £250m in player sales but signed eight players aged 24 or under, with much enthusiasm over the big-money arrivals of Nico Gonzalez and Matias Fernandez-Pardo .

"If you want to be a successful club in the Premier League, you have to trade players and if you don't the chances are you won't be a successful club in the Premier League," said Wilson.

"This is what we've got to do. And if you don't do it, then just keep the squad you've got and forevermore they'll grow old, achieve less and leave for nothing."

The outlook is shaped by Newcastle being fined £5.2m for breaching UEFA's financial sustainability regulations, with £6m suspended pending future compliance.

They have not qualified for Europe this season, and chief financial officer Simon Capper has forecast the club will be "compliant" with the more relaxed Premier League financial rules.

Woltemade exit allowed Fernandez-Pardo signing

Wilson and Capper also revealed that club-record signing Nick Woltemade had to leave on loan to allow the arrival of Fernandez-Pardo.

On Deadline Day, Woltemade, who joined last summer in a £69m deal, moved to Juventus on loan, with Newcastle confirming the £51m signing of Fernandez-Pardo from Lille.

Wilson said: "Because we try to link things together, the ultimate deal for Fernandez-Pardo was only possible because we did the Woltemade deal. The ultimate [Fernandez-Pardo] deal.

"If we didn't do the Woltemade deal, we might have done another deal, but that's what we mean by linking things together."

Capper added: "So the conversation we were having internally was, 'If you want to do that [sign Fernandez-Pardo] you're going to have to give me something back…otherwise we'll be in a position we're not comfortable with'.

"We managed to get that. That's how we work together as a group, as a senior management team, to deliver the best result we can out of a transfer window."

articles.title: Fermín: "Las burlas sobre mi físico me hicieron dudar de mí mismo"
articles.standfirst: El medio alza la voz contra el acoso escolar en un proyecto de la Fundación ColaCao
articles.summary: El medio alza la voz contra el acoso escolar en un proyecto de la Fundación ColaCao
articles.body: Fermín López no es un futbolista corriente. Está acostumbrado a sobreponerse a los reveses, como lo hizo, por ejemplo, hace unos meses tras la fractura que sufrió en un dedo del pie derecho que le dejó sin Mundial. Pero ahora hemos sabido que también tuvo que afrontar una adolescencia difícil marcada por los comentarios dañinos que recibía por su baja estatura, y que llegaron a afectarle, seriamente, a nivel anímico, psicológico, social... El centrocampista de Barça es uno de los deportistas que alza la voz contra el acoso escolar y ofrece su franco testimonio en el proyecto audiovisual Entrenando contra el bullying, impulsado, junto a varios organismos, por la Fundación ColaCao. El internacional, comprometido en la lucha contra el acoso, se sincera, sin tapujos y de forma honesta, con MARCA sobre su experiencia. P. ¿Qué implica para usted colaborar con la Fundación ColaCao en este proyecto contra el bullying? R. Para mí es un honor y una responsabilidad aportar mi granito de arena en esta iniciativa de la Fundación Colacao. Creo que soy una persona que tiene una cierta repercusión y puedo dar un poco más de visibilidad a este proyecto, y estoy muy contento por ello. Y muy orgulloso. P. Porque usted, además, puede hablar desde su propia experiencia. Vivió una situación difícil cuando era adolescente. Explíquenos en qué consistieron los comentarios que sufrió y cómo fue aquella triste experiencia... R. Bueno, tuve alguna que otra burla, por mi estatura y por mi físico, que me hizo sentir inferior durante mi etapa formativa. Fue una etapa complicada y la pude superar gracias a mi familia y a la gente que me quería y quiere. Tuve un momento complicado por mi físico. Siempre había la broma de “Fermín, el pequeñín”. Al principio, te hace gracia y parece que la broma no te afecta porque no te lo tomas mal, pero ya cuando te lo dicen muchas veces sí que lo hace... P. ¿Cómo le afectó? R. Piensas que no puedes competir con gente de tu edad, que no tienes las mismas fuerzas, que eres más bajito.... Esa situación te hace sentir inferior y te genera inseguridad. Ver que no llegas te hace sufrir. Te aislas también, de los compañeros. Pasé muchos momentos duros en la habitación. La angustia va por dentro. Veía que mi momento no llegaba... los demás jugaban y yo no. Mis compañeros parecían hombres y yo no... fue una época dura. P. Y lo sufrió, además, a una edad complicada. Sobre los 14 y 16 años, cuando uno se está definiendo... ¿Cómo le marcó? ¿Cree que le afectó a nivel de carácter y le ha hecho ser diferente? R. Sí, porque al final todos esos malos momentos me los llevo de aprendizaje, y, aunque era muy pequeño y quizás emocionalmente no tenía cierta madurez, creo que ahora lo veo de una manera de aprendizaje. Me ha ayudado a madurar y a ser la persona que soy hoy en día. P. Se aisló, le generó inseguridad, frustración y ansiedad..., pero ¿por las burlas llegó a plantearse dejar el fútbol o dudó de su carrera como futbolista? R. No, no dudé sobre mi carrera, pero sí que muchas veces dudé de mí mismo porque tenía un hándicap que era mi físico, y veía que no podía hacer lo mismo que mis compañeros o que no llegaba a hacer el fútbol que a mí me gustaba. Y, entonces, fue un momento de gran frustración, causado por todos esos pensamientos negativos que tenía por mi físico. P. A pesar de que se aisló, como hacen otros muchos niños y jóvenes que sufren bullying, comenta que tenía el apoyo de su familia. Supongo que el decirlo, el trasladar esa situación a la gente más cercana, es clave para salir de ese pozo en el que un joven se puede meter. R. Sí, es muy importante transmitirlo a los demás, sacarlo de dentro. Y, en mi caso, tenía a mi familia, a mis padres... que eran con los que más me desahogaba. Ellos me transmitían más positividad y me ayudaron a revertir un poco esa situación mala que estaba viviendo. Siempre me salvaban y hacía que no me hundiera. Soltaba con ellos lo que llevaba dentro y por ellos sacaba también las fuerzas cuando no tenía ganas de entrenarme. P. Imagino a gente de La Masía también le ayudó a superarlo, ¿qué profesionales, compañeros o técnicos fueron su gran apoyo? R. En La Masía, tanto con los educadores como con todos los compañeros que tuve allí, siempre me sentí muy querido. Me apoyaban mucho en ese sentido, y al final era un entorno muy familiar para mí y gracias a ellos podía también sobrellevarlo. Me daban un abrazo cuando lo necesité. Aunque estaba lejos de mi familia, les tenía a ellos, que eran como tener otra familia cerca, para poder revertir esta situación o este momento malo que estaba viviendo. P. Tuvo que hacer muy joven un gran esfuerzo mental... R. Sí, yo cogía esos comentarios y los tomaba como una motivación. Que un técnico no me ponga porque soy pequeño o que me digan que soy bajito no me quitará la ilusión ni los sueños ni la motivación. Me hacía luchar más y esforzarme más. Pensaba que algún día lo conseguiría y que se acordarían de mí. Y eso le diría a los niños que ahora lo están pasando mal. P. ¿Qué consejo le daría a un joven que ahora le esté escuchando, leyendo o viendo y está viviendo una situación similar o parecida ya sea en el colegio, en el equipo de fútbol...? R. El consejo que le daría es que, a pesar de la situación mala que esté pasando, nunca dude de sí mismo y que escuche y haga caso sólo a la gente que le quiere de verdad. Y también le diría que sobre todo exteriorice todos los problemas o pensamientos negativos que tenga para que le puedan ayudar, sus seres queridos o su gente cercana. Tienen que saber que todos tenemos unas cualidades muy buenas y creo todos nos debemos rodear de gente que nos quiera de verdad. Les diría que tienes que quererte a ti mismo. Deben creer en ellos. Yo era pequeño, recibí esos comentarios, y he podido cumplir mis sueños. Da igual como seas. P. ¿Y qué le diría a ese niño que es el que hace los comentarios dañinos o que acosa? R. Principalmente, le diría que tuviera un poco de empatía, porque puede ser que le esté pareciendo una simple broma o burla, pero no sabe cómo le va a afectar a la otra persona. Le diría que sobre todo se ponga en el lugar de la otra persona porque cualquier simple comentario puede hacerle sentir inferior o generarle inseguridades. P. Tengo entendido que la referencia de Messi y Iniesta también le sirvió. Le ayudó para superar esa difícil etapa. ¿Cómo fue ese apoyo indirecto? P. Ellos son mis referentes, principalmente por cómo eran como futbolistas y lo que hacían en el campo. Pero también creo que han tenido una infancia o adolescencia parecida a la mía en cuanto al físico. Y en aquellos momentos un poco complicados, ver a dos personas que han sido tan grandes, los mejores del mundo, y han podido revertir situación, hizo que me viera reflejado en ellos. Me hicieron ver que ser pequeño no tiene por qué hacerte sentir inferior. Al contrario, puedes desarrollar otras cualidades futbolísticas que te pueden ayudar: rapidez a la hora de tomar decisiones... Me han ayudado a nunca dudar de mí mismo y a creer que podía llegar a conseguir mis sueños. P. El acoso escolar es una lacra que padecen miles de niños: algunos estudios señalan que en 2025, en España, lo sufrió el 12,3% del alumnado. Pero ¿cree que ahora el bullying, o las burlas, se visibilizan más? R. Creo que ahora mismo se da un poco más de visibilidad y la gente es más consciente de ello y de la importancia de visibilizarlo, pero aún queda mucho trabajo para erradicar todo eso. Hay que trabajar en ello y lograr, además, que todos los niños que lo sufran puedan visibilizarlo y que no se lo guarden dentro. P. ¿Y qué papel considera usted que juegan las redes sociales? Hay más visibilidad de la problemática, pero también más herramientas para acosar, como el ciberbullying y la IA ¿no cree? R. Si. Cada vez estamos más informados de lo que implica el uso de las redes sociales. Y tienen un uso muy dañino también para el bullying. Son muy dañinas porque lo multiplican todo por mil. Llega a mucha gente, y, además, desde una pantalla puedes hacer cosas muy peligrosas para un niño, para una persona que lo está pasando mal. Cualquier comentario puede generar inseguridad o hacer sentir a otra persona inferior y hacerle pasar un mal momento. Un simple comentario puede hacer mucho daño. P. ¿Piensa que el acoso es una problemática estructural en la sociedad? ¿Qué medidas tomaría para erradicarlo? R. No es fácil, pero creo que deberíamos ponernos todas las personas a ello, a intentar acabar con el acoso. Hay que educar en buenos valores. Hay que trabajarlo en las familias, en el colegio, en los clubes, en cualquier ámbito deportivo o social. El esfuerzo para erradicar el bullying debe ser conjunto. De todos. Pienso que poco a poco se da más visibilidad y se va erradicando y la gente es más consciente, pero considero que aún queda mucho camino por recorrer, y, te insisto, los clubes, las familias, el colegio... deberíamos seguir transmitiendo valores como el respeto y la empatía para que ya desde pequeños se pueda ir erradicando. P. Hace unos meses vivimos también la experiencia con las redes sociales de Roland Araujo, que recibió muchas críticas y pasó por un momento difícil que acabó con su retiro del fútbol durante un mes. Muchos jugadores o personajes públicos adultos también han tenido que cerrar sus cuentas. ¿Cómo vivió todo aquello que le pasó también a Araujo? R. Es duro porque es un compañero y era un amigo dentro del vestuario, y ver que estaba pasando esa situación mala por comentarios o por las redes sociales, duele. Pero considero que los clubes, los vestuarios... son muy importantes, y es un entorno también familiar y nosotros intentamos ayudarle a que él pudiera seguir adelante y superar ese momento. P. ¿Cómo se protege usted de todo el daño que causan los insultos y los comentarios dañinos en las redes? R. Sobre todo, apoyándome en la gente de mi entorno. En mi familia, en mis amigos, en mi pareja... y después sé que hay que relativizar un poco las cosas externas o las cosas de las redes sociales porque al final es un comentario que pone alguien desde una pantalla que no te conoce y no sabe nada de tu historia ni sabe tu día a día. Entonces creo que tienes que relativizar un poco esos comentarios y también hacer un trabajo emocional para que eso no te afecte. P. Pero aunque los que insultan no tienen justificación ni necesitan motivos que motiven sus críticas, supongo que ahora sólo recibirá elogios por su gran inicio de temporada... R. Bueno, ahora estoy contento porque he vuelto a jugar con mi equipo, y estoy haciendo goles. Ha sido un verano complicado, pero ya ha pasado todo y estoy contento de poder volver a hacer lo que me gusta y disfrutar en el campo.

articles.title: Leicester City crisis: Russell Martin under pressure at Foxes
articles.summary: Former Leicester City defender Conor Coady says the problems at his old club "have got to run deeper" than the manager and players.
articles.body:
Former Leicester City defender Conor Coady believes the problems at his old club "have got to run deeper" than the manager and players after their difficult start to life in League One.

The former England international revealed he could feel the decline during his two-season spell in the East Midlands.

Leicester are 18th with five points from their opening five matches and were beaten 4-0 at home by Oxford United on Saturday.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club , Coady said the club had been "in transition too long" following three relegations in the past four seasons.

"There's got to be something deep down that's wrong here because it's been going on for too many years," he added.

"Everyone will sit there and go 'the players aren't good enough'. They haven't been good enough. I was there, I felt it, I wasn't good enough when I was there.

Latest Leicester news, analysis and fan views

Listen to Leicester City content on BBC Sounds

Coady joined the Foxes for a reported £8.5m in 2023 following eight years with Wolves but left for Wrexham after two seasons.

He believes Leicester have lost the identity that once made them one of the most difficult sides to face at King Power Stadium and led to the famous Premier League title in 2016 and the FA Cup win in 2021.

Recalling teams containing the likes of Jamie Vardy, James Maddison, Youri Tielemans, Wilfred Ndidi, Wes Morgan and Robert Huth, he added: "It was one of the hardest games you were going to have in a season.

"I just feel like that identity has been lost over the years. I was part of that team when we lost that identity."

Last season, Leicester City owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha told BBC Sport he shouldered the blame for the club's decline - and he has since put the club on the market with an asking price of more than £200m.

'There doesn't seem to be a strategy' - Smith

Observer football journalist Rory Smith questioned Leicester's recent managerial appointments and whether there is a clear long-term strategy at the club.

He pointed to the differing styles of Leicester's recent managers and said it "doesn't suggest there's any real strategy" or an "overarching belief" from the ownership about what the club should be.

Smith also believes expectations will make patience difficult, with Leicester regarded as one of the biggest clubs in League One.

"They should have the quality to be relatively competitive within League One regardless," he said.

'That's a sackable performance' - what next for Martin at Leicester?

Oxford loss 'solely down to the players' - Souttar

Coady believes Leicester did make progress over the summer by refreshing the squad and giving opportunities to younger players.

But he said the appointment of Russell Martin requires patience because of the time needed to implement his style of football.

"They've decided to bring Russell in, so you decide to tie your flag to the mast and go, 'right, we are going to go with this'," Coady said.

"If they're going to make a decision after four or five games, there was no point in bringing Russell in because that's not the sort of manager he is."

'Martin needs a result quickly' - Sutton

Former Blackburn Rovers striker Chris Sutton believes Martin's reputation for possession-based football could make his position increasingly difficult if results do not improve.

"There is this perception now which is following him around of his teams just being purely possession-based and all about keeping the ball and not having any thrust or cutting edge," Sutton said.

"The job he's gone into at Leicester, because of the expectation this season, is for them to bounce straight back."

Smith argued Martin's reputation could also mean supporters are less willing to give him time, despite his previous success in guiding Southampton to promotion from the Championship.

Sutton agreed the criticism of Martin following his short spell at Rangers had not always been fair, but said Leicester's ambitions leave little room for a slow start.

"He needs a result or two quickly to turn the tide," Sutton added.

"Leicester fans expect the team to go up, and that's his biggest problem."

articles.title: Y Sucic se autorregaló un gol para ganar
articles.standfirst: El croata celebra hoy su vigesimocuarto cumpleaños en su mejor momento en la Real, tras hacer dos tantos en cinco jornadas, el de ayer para sumar tres valiosos puntos en Elche
articles.summary: El croata celebra hoy su vigesimocuarto cumpleaños en su mejor momento en la Real, tras hacer dos tantos en cinco jornadas, el de ayer para sumar tres valiosos puntos en Elche
articles.body: Luka Sucic celebra hoy su vigesimocuarto cumpleaños y ayer en Elche se hizo uno de los mejores regalos posibles: marcó el gol con el que le dio la victoria a la Real Sociedad y el poder pasar hoy un día mucho más feliz que si no la hubiera logrado. El talentoso centrocampista croata ya había hecho un tanto en el Santiago Bernabéu y con el segundo se convierte en el inesperado pichichi momentáneo del conjunto txuriurdin. Sucic volvió en Elche al equipo titular de la Real, después de quedarse fuera el jueves frente al Celta, y cuando no se había llegado al cuarto de hora de partido obligó a Dituro a hacer una gran intervención, ante un potente disparo de los suyos. Después sufrió la mejoría local antes del descanso y después se dejó ver de nuevo, marcando el 0-3, aunque al final no subió al marcador por la mano previa de Jon Martín al inicio de la jugada y la muy discutible roja al 6 txuriurdin. Al croata le tocó luego ponerse el buzo de trabajo cuando la Real jugó con uno menos y sufrir el empate a dos de los locales y su posterior ofensiva en busca del triunfo. Cuando parecía que lo iban a poder lograr, realizó una gran conducción en una contra y, tras salvar una dura entrada de un rival y regatear a otros dos, firmó un golazo para que el que terminó siendo el 2-3 definitivo. Sucic, que ya dio algún síntoma de mejoría tras la llegada de Matarazzo, con una gran actuación en la final de Copa, la mejor desde que aterrizó en San Sebastián en 2024, ha empezado bien esta temporada y, tras su gol en el 4-1 del Bernabéu, hizo el segundo el Elche para poder celebrar un triunfo justo unas horas antes de su cumpleaños, así que no pudo hacerse mejor autorregalo. El reto del 24 de la plantilla txuriurdin es dar continuidad a este buen inicio de temporada, siendo también más regular en los partidos, y dejar patente la gran calidad que viene mostrando en algunas ocasiones y que fue por la que la Real pagó por él 12 millones de euros, con el objetivo de que diera un paso adelante más en su carrera y su nivel permitiese una venta por mucho más dinero que ese.
