articles.title: Mourinho recupera a Tchouaméni, Thiago Pitarch y Endrick
articles.standfirst: Novedades en una lista ante el Inter con ocho bajas y cuatro canteranos
articles.summary: El técnico tiene siete bajas y convoca a tres canteranos
articles.body: El Real Madrid ha facilitado la lista de convocados para el partido de esta noche ante el Inter. Una convocatoria en la que la novedad la protagonizan Thiago Pitarch, Tchouaméni y Endrick, que vuelven a estar a las órdenes de Mourinho un vez recuperados de las lesiones que les han tenido de baja desde la pretemporada. Tres refuerzos para el banquillo que ayudarán a amortiguar la extensa lista de bajas, con Militao, Mendy, Rodrygo y Asencio lesionados; Camavinga, Bernardo Silva y Güler, sancionados; y Lunin, con un proceso gripal . Ocho ausencias en total. Por ello, Mou ha vuelto a tirar del Castilla para completar la convocatoria y se lleva al estreno de Champios a los metas Sergio Mestre y Javi Navarro, el defensa Mario Rivas y el centrocampista Cestero. Este último, incluso, tiene opciones de ser titular en un centro del campo en el que sólo está disponible para iniciar Fede Valverde. Lunin, ausente en el último entrenamiento antes del duelo ante el Inter por un proceso gripal, no se ha recuperado a tiempo y causa bajan también. CONVOCATORIA DEL REAL MADRID ANTE EL INTER Porteros: Courtois, Sergio Mestre y Javi Navarro. Defensas: Huijsen, Trent, Konaté, Cucurella, Carreras, Rüdiger, Dumfries y Mario Rivas. Centrocampistas: Bellingham, Valverde, Tchouaméni, Thiago Pitarch y Cestero. Delanteros: Vinicius, Endrick, Mbappé, Espí, Brahim y Diomande.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Rankings after Week 1
articles.summary: While the Heisman Trophy is never won in September, a hot start to the college football season is nevertheless a welcome sign.
articles.body:
While the Heisman Trophy is never won in September, a hot start to the college football season is nevertheless a welcome sign.

In 2026, many of the expected contenders eased into the campaign. Whether it was against a lower-division opponent or Group of Six program, a bunch of key players had a gaudy opening week.

But the competition is quickly set to rise, especially for Texas and Ohio State.

This early in the campaign, any ranking is heavily contingent on the intent. You could try to predict the season, focus on actual on-field production alone or land somewhere in between. This is essentially the third option.

Week 1 performance matters to this order, but some notable preseason candidates are still mentioned even if they weren't downright amazing in their opener.

Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida : If the Gators rise behind first-year coach Jon Sumrall, it's fair to anticipate Jadan Baugh is a key reason. He opened the campaign with 160 yards and three touchdowns in a 66-21 win over Florida Atlantic.

Rocco Becht, QB, Penn State : In three seasons as Iowa State's starter, Becht peaked at three touchdown passes. So, naturally, his debut at Penn State featured four scores as Penn State blanked Marshall 45-0. Becht has a couple favorable games on the horizon with Temple and Buffalo up next.

Mason Heintschel, QB, Pitt : The competition qualifier exists here, but throwing for 453 yards and seven touchdowns in a rout of Miami (Ohio) is pretty darn impressive. Heintschel should face a stiffer test at home against UCF in Week 2.

Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee: True freshman QB Faizon Brandon accounted for five touchdowns in a 56-9 triumph over Furman. On the defensive side, though, the Vols saw Penn State transfer Xavier Gilliam amass five tackles for loss and three sacks. Obviously, that's not sustainable. But he deserves a mention.

Keelon Russell, Alabama : In his first career start, Russell threw for 256 yards and added 86 yards with a touchdown on the ground. He showed composure and explosiveness in a 48-10 blowout of East Carolina.

Gunner Stockton, Georgia : Stockton had a near-perfect afternoon as Georgia blew out Tennessee State 63-3. He completed 15 of 16 passes for 202 yards and three touchdowns, only playing one possession in the second half.

Josh Hoover, Indiana : The transfer from TCU impressed in his IU debut, ending the 52-16 win over North Texas with a 13-of-16 line for 231 yards and four scores.

Sam Leavitt, LSU : Unfortunately for Leavitt, he tossed an interception on LSU's first drive. Fortunately for Leavitt, that was the lone blemish. He passed for 230 yards, scampered for 113 and accounted for three touchdowns in a 51-10 smackdown of Clemson.

CJ Carr, Notre Dame : Carr, a preseason front-runner, didn't exactly shine in prime time. A garbage-time touchdown boosted his 19-of-29 line, which included 239 yards and two scores. He was good, not great. But it's plenty early.

Julian Sayin, Ohio State : No problems for Sayin in Week 1. While the Buckeyes stormed past Ball State 56-3, he hit 21-of-25 passes for 320 yards and three touchdowns while adding a fourth score on the ground.

Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss : Following a quiet opening half with two giveaways, Chambliss erupted to nudge Ole Miss past Louisville 41-38. He threw for 336 yards, rushed for 60 and totaled four touchdowns.

Jayden Maiava, USC : Through two games, Maiava has connected on 48-of-54 attempts with six total touchdowns and zero interceptions. That, my friends, is good.

Early on? Yikes. It's a good thing the game doesn't end after 15 minutes.

After a scoreless first quarter, Dante Moore settled in and helped Oregon dig out of a surprising 10-point hole to Boise State. The offense rattled off five straight scoring drives en route to a 34-27 victory.

Moore completed 28-of-37 attempts for a career-best 387 yards, tossing three touchdowns with no turnovers.

"I thought Dante, from my seat, played extremely well," Oregon coach Dan Lanning told reporters afterward.

Considering how many other mistakes the Ducks made, Moore's play was the main reason they escaped the scare against Boise State.

Arch Manning opened the 2025 campaign as the most-hyped quarterback in the country, and September was very unkind to him.

This year, he's off to a much better start.

Manning hit 20-of-27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns, leading the Longhorns to a 59-7 rout of Texas State.

Yes, the red-zone interception he threw was a horrid decision. He either tried to squeeze a ball into triple coverage or didn't anticipate that two defenders could close the window so quickly. There's no excusing that.

Overall, though, Manning opened with a strong performance. He'll be tested next weekend in a prime-time showdown at home against Ohio State.

After bursting onto the radar at Tulane and propelling Duke to an ACC title, Darian Mensah has already proved his worth.

Week 1, however, showed a glimpse of what he might be able to accomplish with Miami this season. The supporting cast for Mensah—even as the 'Canes rebuild their offensive line—has elite upside.

Miami smoked Stanford 42-6 behind a massive debut from Mensah. He completed 27-of-30 attempts with 401 yards, five touchdowns and zero turnovers.

Expect another gaudy stat line in Week 2, as well.

Thursday night, the Hurricanes host lower-division Florida A&M. Mensah presumably won't play all game, but Miami will likely be throwing early and often.

Jeremiah Smith did exactly what you'd expect from him opposite Ball State.

During the first half, he racked up eight receptions for 151 yards and two scores. Smith straight-up dominated one touchdown drive, reeling in five passes and capping the possession in the end zone.

Smith (metaphorically) kicked back and watched the last 30 minutes while Ohio State cruised to a 56-3 win. The team wanted to ensure his health for Week 2.

In short: That was a smart move. The trip to Texas is far more important than adding a few catches for award purposes.

And it's a pretty nice opportunity for a Heisman moment, too.

I'm not entirely certain what Stanford was trying to prove, but an evening full of one-on-one coverage for Malachi Toney didn't work out well.

Miami's star sophomore had 12 receptions for a program-record 234 yards , scoring three touchdowns, striking the Heisman pose after each one. Toney didn't play in the fourth quarter, either.

As mentioned with Mensah, Thursday's game against Florida A&M should be friendly. Miami will probably pepper Toney with touches right away.

I might suggest you consider a second man in coverage, FAMU.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for College Football's Top QBs after Week 1
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included is each player's production through the air and on the ground, the outcome of their game and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight quality of opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F, and those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Who's ready for a whole bunch of "A" grades against overmatched opponents?

Week 1 Passing Stats: 26-of-36, 430 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 33 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Florida State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (27-24)

A year after throwing 13 interceptions to lead the ACC and rank third in the nation, Kevin Jennings had a tough time taking care of the football once again with a pair of picks in an ugly win against Florida State.

Still, 430 passing yards is 430 passing yards, and a win is a win. It's also worth mentioning that Jennings looked far more mobile after being slowed by a foot injury for much of the 2025 season, so expect more dual-threat production.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 20-of-30, 305 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 30 yards, 1 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Oregon State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (33-20)

Conner Weigman kicked off the season with a 305-yard passing performance, but it was his one-yard touchdown run with 5:01 remaining in the fourth quarter that sealed the victory for Houston after Oregon State had made it a one-possession game.

He had 700 rushing yards and 11 scores on the ground a year ago, and his dual-threat ability is a big reason the Cougars were No. 23 in the preseason AP poll.

18. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, California

Week 1 Passing Stats: 24-of-41, 271 yards, 2 TD, 2 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, -16 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (UCLA) Week 1 Outcome: Loss (24-45)

UCLA hung 21 unanswered points on California to turn a tie game heading into the fourth quarter into a blowout loss, and Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele threw a pair of interceptions in that decisive final stretch that both led to Bruins touchdowns.

The first giveaway snapped a program-record streak of 212 consecutive pass attempts without an interception, and to his credit, he played through an apparent leg injury and a collapsing pocket for much of the game.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 24-of-35, 268 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 61 yards, 1 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Washington State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (24-10)

While many of the nation's top quarterbacks started the season with a cupcake, Demond Williams Jr. was thrown straight into the Apple Cup, albeit with the Huskies installed as 23.5-point favorites.

He completed all six of his pass attempts for 110 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter to help put a close game out of reach, and he did a good job picking his spots to run without putting himself in harm's way.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 21-of-30, 233 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 20 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Missouri State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (50-0)

Marcel Reed played just over three quarters in the blowout win against Missouri State, but that was enough time for him to build a 40-0 lead before heading to the sidelines.

He looked in control of the offense throughout the game, and showed some nice early chemistry with high-profile transfer Isaiah Horton (4 catches, 76 yards, 1 TD), who spent last season at Alabama after three years at Miami.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 11-of-17, 225 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 7 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (UTEP) Week 1 Outcome: Win (51-0)

A healthy John Mateer has a chance to do some special things for the Oklahoma Sooners this season if his start to last season was any indication before he suffered a hand injury and never quite returned to form.

Lighting up UTEP for three quarters doesn't prove much, but seeing his three touchdown passes go for 40, 34 and 48 yards did provide a glimpse into the offense's big-play potential.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 16-of-28, 230 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 113 yards, 2 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Clemson) Week 1 Outcome: Win (51-10)

Sam Leavitt had almost two hours of extra time to sit and think about his LSU debut after a lightning delay pushed kickoff back, then he promptly threw an incompletion and an interception on his first two pass attempts in a Tigers uniform.

With that out of his system, he then went to work showcasing his dynamic dual-threat talents, racking up 343 total yards and three touchdowns in a shocking blowout victory where he looked like the best player on the field.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 22-of-29, 262 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 24 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Northern Arizona) Week 1 Outcome: Win (35-7)

Noah Fifita displayed the accuracy, efficiency and command of the offense that has made him a standout during his time at Arizona in a comfortable victory over Northern Arizona.

The running game was the focal point against an overmatched defense, as the Wildcats tallied 206 yards and three touchdowns on 35 carries, leaving him with slightly less gaudy numbers than some of his counterparts.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 29-of-49, 241 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT

Week 1 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 3 yards

One of the top quarterbacks in the transfer portal, Drew Mestemaker followed head coach Eric Morris from North Texas to Oklahoma State following a 2025 season where he had an FBS-leading 4,379 yards and 34 touchdowns.

His Cowboys debut was an unmitigated disaster. He threw two picks and never looked comfortable in the pocket as Oklahoma State, a 13.5-point favorite, suffered a Week 1 loss.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 13-of-16, 231 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 0 carries, 0 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (North Texas) Week 1 Outcome: Win (52-16)

On the first pass attempt of his Indiana career, Josh Hoover found fellow high-profile transfer Nick Marsh in the end zone, and he hauled in the touchdown reception with a highlight-reel, one-handed grab.

Just like that, the page was turned from the Fernando Mendoza era, and facing off against a solid North Texas team, this certainly looked like a Hoosiers offense capable of putting up some gaudy numbers once again.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 26-of-35, 259 yards, 0 TD, 3 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 21 carries, 27 yards, 1 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Baylor) Week 1 Outcome: Win (17-16)

The Auburn Tigers escaped with a Week 1 victory thanks to a goal-line stand on a two-point conversion attempt by Baylor in the final seconds, but Byrum Brown's debut was a mess.

After throwing a career-high three interceptions and being rendered a non-factor in the running game, he did step up in the clutch. Brown led a 10-play, 75-yard drive late in the fourth quarter, and capped it off with an 11-yard touchdown run to give Auburn a 17-10 lead with 3:21 remaining.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 15-of-16, 202 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 0 carries, 0 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Tennessee State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (63-3)

To say that Georgia was not tested by Tennessee State would be an understatement, and Gunner Stockton faced little resistance picking apart the Tigers secondary.

He led five straight touchdown drives to start the game before heading to the sidelines midway through the second quarter on an extremely hot day where it was 101 degrees at kickoff.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 13-of-18, 176 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 31 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Idaho) Week 1 Outcome: Win (66-14)

Expectations are high for Devon Dampier this season following an injury-plagued but still highly productive first season at Utah a year ago, and he was on cruise control against Idaho in the season opener on Thursday night.

He had double-digit rushing attempts in 10 of his 12 games a year ago, and being more selective with when he tucks the ball and puts his body in jeopardy will go a long way in keeping him closer to 100 percent for a full season.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 19-of-29, 239 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, -6 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Wisconsin) Week 1 Outcome: Win (41-13)

Notre Dame had a tougher time than the final score suggests facing off against Wisconsin at Lambeau Field on Sunday night, as it was a 27-13 game heading into the fourth quarter.

CJ Carr led an eight-play, 75-yard drive and a 12-play, 88-yard drive in the fourth quarter that both found the end zone to put the game out of reach. His 29 passes against 32 rushing attempts are a good indication he will be shouldering more of the offensive load this year after leaning heavily on Jeremiyah Love in 2025.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 23-of-25, 349 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT

Week 1 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -2 yards

Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Fresno State)

Jayden Maiava already has two games under his belt this season, as USC picked up a 42-26 victory over San Jose State as part of the abbreviated Week 0 slate, and he has been prolific thus far to put it mildly.

In two lopsided victories, he has completed 48-of-54 pass attempts for 635 yards and five touchdowns, averaging a staggering 11.8 yards per attempt.

Maiava has developed some early chemistry with 4-star freshman Trent Mosley (11 catches, 222 yards, 3 TD), who is tasked with replacing All-American Makai Lemon.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 28-of-37, 378 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, -5 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Boise State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (34-27)

It took Dante Moore and the Oregon offense some time to settle in against a good Boise State defense, and they went scoreless on four of their first five drives in a game that was close right down to the final horn.

A 62-yard touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore with 7:51 remaining in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning strike, though it came with a lot of yards after catch. Those were the few minor holes to be poked in what was, at the end of the day, a 378-yard, three-touchdown performance against a team many expect to make the College Football Playoff.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 27-of-30, 401 yards, 5 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 5 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Stanford) Week 1 Outcome: Win (45-6)

Darian Mensah entered the season as one of the early Heisman Trophy favorites, and he did nothing to shift that perception with a 401-yard, five-touchdown clinic against Stanford.

If there was a blow to his candidacy, it's the fact that teammate Malachi Toney (12 catches, 234 yards, 3 TD) now looks like an even more viable threat to potentially challenge him for the award. That is a great problem to have if you're a Hurricanes fan.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 20-of-27, 305 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 6 yards Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Texas State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (59-7)

A year ago, Arch Manning started his ballyhooed first season as a starter by completing 17-of-30 attempts for 151 yards with one touchdown and one interception in a loss to Ohio State.

He had some time to warm up this year, albeit against a Texas State squad that has a chance to be one of the better Group of Six teams in the country. Will that lead to a better outcome in his rematch with the Buckeyes this Saturday?

Week 1 Passing Stats: 21-of-25, 320 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -9 yards, 1 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Ball State) Week 1 Outcome: Win (56-3)

The Julian Sayin-to-Jeremiah Smith connection showed zero signs of rust on Saturday, as they connected for eight catches, 151 yards and three touchdowns against an overmatched Ball State secondary.

A year after completing 77 percent of his passes and finishing fourth in Heisman Trophy balloting, Sayin might be the safest bet in the country to have a seat in New York at the end of the year. Whether he can win it will be the bigger debate.

Week 1 Passing Stats: 21-of-36, 336 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 1 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 60 yards, 1 TD Week 1 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Louisville) Week 1 Outcome: Win (41-38)

With 15 incompletions and an interception, it was far from a flawless performance from Trinidad Chambliss in his 2026 debut, but the smile on his face and nod of confidence when he realized he had 1:28 of game time to orchestrate a game-winning drive spoke volumes.

He connected on passes of 15 and 18 yards to help drive the Rebels into field-goal range for what would be the game-winning kick, and Ole Miss gained an early boon to its resume with a victory over a very good Louisville team.

In an effort to keep things fresh and allow for the inclusion of breakout performers, we will be re-ranking the top 20 quarterbacks each week on this final slide. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

With only one game in the books for most of these players, preseason expectations still serve as the backbone of these rankings, though a few new names did creep into the picture at the bottom of the list with a chance to climb with continued success.

1. Darian Mensah, Miami 2. Julian Sayin, Ohio State 3. Jayden Maiava, USC 4. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss 5. Dante Moore, Oregon 6. Sam Leavitt, LSU 7. Arch Manning, Texas 8. CJ Carr, Notre Dame 9. Devon Dampier, Utah 10. Gunner Stockton, Georgia 11. Josh Hoover, Indiana 12. John Mateer, Oklahoma 13. Noah Fifita, Arizona 14. Marcel Reed, Texas A&M 15. Demond Williams Jr., Washington 16. Conner Weigman, Houston 17. Rocco Becht, Penn State 18. Austin Simmons, Missouri 19. Mason Heintschel, Pitt 20. Kevin Jennings, SMU

articles.title: Orient bring in Moldovan midfielder Pascaluta
articles.summary: Leyton Orient sign Moldova Under-21 international Cristian Pascaluta on an initial short-term contract.
articles.body:
Leyton Orient have signed Moldova Under-21 international Cristian Pascaluta on an initial short-term contract.

The 20-year-old midfielder has trained with the O's in recent weeks, and the move is subject to the granting of a work permit.

"I am a midfield player that likes to win the ball for my team and start attacks with my passing ability," Pascaluta told Orient's official website .

"I am going to work extremely hard to try to earn my chance to play."
